title: Monitoring and Evaluation of the Installed Wind Turbine in the Port of Sihanoukville
description: In 2002, a feasibility study was carried out into the available wind energy and the costs and benefits of the installation of a wind turbine in the port of Sihanoukville. In September 2009, the wind turbine was installed at a total study and investment cost of EUR 837,000, to which about 40% was contributed by the MOW department, 25% by the EU Asia Pro Eco Programme and 35% by the Sihanoukville Port Authority. Now, the Port Authority has requested an additional contribution to monitor and evaluate the operation of the wind turbine during two years in cooperation with a Flemish consultancy firm. By actually promoting environment-friendly energy in this developing country, which is fully in line with the priority policy of the Cambodian Government, opportunities were created to apply alternative forms of energy more readily than the traditional thermal plants. By emphasising the environment-friendly aspect of the project, attention is devoted to this country's sustainable development.

title: Strengthening_Math_Results_and_Teaching_SMART
description: General description:  The VVOB 2017-2021 programme in Cambodia will upgrade the capacity of teacher trainers and practice school supervisors at 4 Teacher Education Colleges (TECs) in the provinces of Phnom Penh, Battambang, Kandal and Kampong Cham. Teacher trainers and practice school supervisors will be supported in different ways to upgrade their content knowledge of and pedagogical skills in mathematics, and to manage their classroom to deliver differentiated instruction taking into account learning difficulties and learning disabilities of pupils. All of VVOB's capacity development activities will be gender-sensitive. A total of 120 teacher trainers and 540 practice school supervisors will be directly supported by VVOB's programme. By the end of the programme and each subsequent year, 1,000 student teachers of TECs will benefit from the programme, 6,200 pupils in practice schools will benefit from the upgraded teaching skills of their practice school supervisors, and last but not least, 45,000 pupils will benefit from the upgraded capacities of the student teachers who become teachers in primary schools throughout the country. Finally, the programme will deliver support to upgrade the skills of TEC managers and school leaders of practice schools to evaluate performance and support teacher trainers and teachers, and to manage their colleges and schools in a gender-sensitive and environment-friendly way. --

Teacher trainers and practice school supervisors will be supported in different ways to upgrade their content knowledge of and pedagogical skills in mathematics, and to manage their classroom to deliver differentiated instruction taking into account learning difficulties and learning disabilities of pupils. All of VVOB's capacity development activities will be gender-sensitive. A total of 120 teacher trainers and 540 practice school supervisors will be directly supported by VVOB's programme. By the end of the programme and each subsequent year, 1,000 student teachers of TECs will benefit from the programme, 6,200 pupils in practice schools will benefit from the upgraded teaching skills of their practice school supervisors, and last but not least, 45,000 pupils will benefit from the upgraded capacities of the student teachers who become teachers in primary schools throughout the country. Finally, the programme will deliver support to upgrade the skills of TEC managers and school leaders of practice schools to evaluate performance and support teacher trainers and teachers, and to manage their colleges and schools in a gender-sensitive and environment-friendly way. --

title: Strengthening_Math_Results_and_Teaching_SMART
description: General description:  The VVOB 2017-2021 programme in Cambodia will upgrade the capacity of teacher trainers and practice school supervisors at 4 Teacher Education Colleges (TECs) in the provinces of Phnom Penh, Battambang, Kandal and Kampong Cham. Teacher trainers and practice school supervisors will be supported in different ways to upgrade their content knowledge of and pedagogical skills in mathematics, and to manage their classroom to deliver differentiated instruction taking into account learning difficulties and learning disabilities of pupils. All of VVOB's capacity development activities will be gender-sensitive. A total of 120 teacher trainers and 540 practice school supervisors will be directly supported by VVOB's programme. By the end of the programme and each subsequent year, 1,000 student teachers of TECs will benefit from the programme, 6,200 pupils in practice schools will benefit from the upgraded teaching skills of their practice school supervisors, and last but not least, 45,000 pupils will benefit from the upgraded capacities of the student teachers who become teachers in primary schools throughout the country. Finally, the programme will deliver support to upgrade the skills of TEC managers and school leaders of practice schools to evaluate performance and support teacher trainers and teachers, and to manage their colleges and schools in a gender-sensitive and environment-friendly way. --
implementing_agencies: VVOB - Vlaamse Vereniging voor Ontwikkelingssamenwerking en technische Bijstand
funding_agencies: Directorate General for Co-operation and Development

title: Projet de cooperation universitaire - Initiative Sud 2011 - Mise en ?uvre durable d'approches centr?es sur l'?tudiant dans l'enseignement des sciences au Cambodge
description: Korte projecten (2 jaar) die samenwerkingsvormen mogelijk maken die binnen bestaande VLIR-programma's niet gefinancierd kunnen  worden en dienen als  ''zaaigeld'' voor nieuwe partnerschappen, ''oogstgeld'' van eerdere projecten of ''extensiegeld''  The Science Environmental and Agricultural Life skills Programma (SEAL) in Cambodia aims at improving primary and lower-secondary education for science and life skills subjects by making it less ''rote learning'' and more student centered. Educational resources, methodologies and low-cost activities are developed and localised in order to enhance a more student centered approach in science teaching at basic education level. The programme targets lecturers at the teacher training colleges. Through their teaching they pass the teaching methodology on to student teachers (and future basic education teachers). The programme is supported by VVOB, the Flemish Association for Development Cooperation and Technical Assistance and the Regional Teacher Training Institute in Kandal.The project ''Sustainable implementation of student centered approaches (SCA) in science education in Cambodia aims to increase the impact of the current SEAL programme by 1) scaling up the programme to the level of higher secondary education and 2) by developing and distributing a set of recommendations on the implementation of student centered approaches in science education.  Direct target groups :- National Institute of Education (NIE) lecturers (science and non-science)- Regional Teacher Training institute (RTTC) lecturers ( science and non-science)Indirect target groups :- students at regional teacher training colleges and NIE- students at secondary schools- lecturers at AHS- students at AHS

title: Strengthening_Math_Results_and_Teaching_SMART
description: General description:  The VVOB 2017-2021 programme in Cambodia will upgrade the capacity of teacher trainers and practice school supervisors at 4 Teacher Education Colleges (TECs) in the provinces of Phnom Penh, Battambang, Kandal and Kampong Cham. Teacher trainers and practice school supervisors will be supported in different ways to upgrade their content knowledge of and pedagogical skills in mathematics, and to manage their classroom to deliver differentiated instruction taking into account learning difficulties and learning disabilities of pupils. All of VVOB's capacity development activities will be gender-sensitive. A total of 120 teacher trainers and 540 practice school supervisors will be directly supported by VVOB's programme. By the end of the programme and each subsequent year, 1,000 student teachers of TECs will benefit from the programme, 6,200 pupils in practice schools will benefit from the upgraded teaching skills of their practice school supervisors, and last but not least, 45,000 pupils will benefit from the upgraded capacities of the student teachers who become teachers in primary schools throughout the country. Finally, the programme will deliver support to upgrade the skills of TEC managers and school leaders of practice schools to evaluate performance and support teacher trainers and teachers, and to manage their colleges and schools in a gender-sensitive and environment-friendly way. --

title: F.a: Cambodia Changemaker Network (CCN)
description: In Cambodia 65 % of the population is under age of 30 and therefore youth empowerment is an imperative. While youth is dynamic resource, there is little representation of young people in decision-making process. Robust youth participation is perhaps the strongest mechanism to enable their potential contribute to the development of their community. By building capacity among Cambodian youth, Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) is empowering the next generation of leaders and agents of change.Objectives: To enhance space and opportunities for youth to be actively involved in the society and policy making process  To increase knowledge, skills and awareness of youth on human rights, education and peaceExpected Result:  Youth have enhanced knowledge and capacity to constructively engage in advocacy actions Youth have increased opportunity and spaces to express their voices on their concerned issues Strengthened youth organisation and networkingRights-holders/beneficiaries:Cambodia Changemaker Network has identified the core to establish the network in 2014. During 2015 this group has been growing to more than 100 members with diverse background including high school students, university students, monks, disabled, and staff from different NGOs and public sector. Many of them are from Phnom Penh city, and some smaller numbers are from provinces including Kom Pong Spue, Bonteay Meanchey, Kompong Cham, Siem Reap, Battam Bong, Kandal, and Prey Veng. Implementing partner: Khmer Youth Association (KYA) was a hosting partner for Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) in 2015, but for 2016 CNN members have agreed to have FCA as the hosting partner. FCA is able to provide effective administration and other technical support to the network as needed.

title: F.a: Community-based support for children with disabilities
description: The project enhances the rights of children with severe disabilities by training communities and their leaders on disability issues and the rights of persons with disabilities, by supporting community based day centres and schools as well as home based care, in Kampot and Kratie provinces. Children with disabilities in Cambodia and their families often live in poverty. Only 3% of disabled children start school and more than half of them drop out soon. Countryside is almost totally lacking educational and supporting services for severely disabled children and ignorance and discriminating attitudes cause enormous barriers to their wellbeing. Without the support of community, parents and authorities the children don't have possibility to develop their skills physically, socially or educationally. However, the work of the project implementer Komar Pikar Foundation (KPF) has proved that by community based solutions even the severely disabled children and their families can have access to education and supporting services and the discrimination can be reduced. As result of the project the children with severe disabilities are accepted as part of their communities, they have possibility to learn and develop their skills and have better access to e.g. health services. The financial status of the families improves and discrimination is reduced.

title: Frame agreement with NGO (Operation a Day's Work)
description: The project  We protect children, do you? - Promoting Child Rights and Protecting Children from the Worst Forms of Child Labour in Cambodia  focuses on the prevention of child labor and the protection of children involved in the worst forms of child labor, in particular, children engaged in domestic work, brick factories and the entertainment industry. According to the recent statistics, there are 1,4 million working children in Cambodia. Within the most dangerous forms of labor, the working conditions are extremely damaging to health. Thousands of children lack opportunities for education because of being forced to work. This results to a cycle of illiteracy and poverty. In Cambodia, the society doesn't recognize the need to protect children from exploitation and significant gaps do exist in official child protection structures, which makes it important for NGOs to contribute in this field.The project opposes child labor exploitation by developing groups and networks in different community sectors to monitor, investigate and refer to child rights (CR) violations. Wider audience is reached through activities that disseminate information on CR and on how to correctly respond to violations. The project also aims to contribute to the prevention of CR violations in Cambodia and to the protection and rehabilitation of victims of the violations.The project is located in both rural and urban areas in Phnom Penh and its surroundings and the provinces of Kandal, Koh Kong, Preah Sihanouk and Siem Reap.The first project phase has been successful in establishing local level Child Protection Groups (PG), especially Child PGs in the target communities. The public awareness and debate about Child Rights and risks of the Child Labour is also increasing. title: F.a: Preventing sexual abuse of boys
description: The issue of male victims of sexual exploitation is a silenced problem in Cambodia. Therefore it is difficult for the victims to seek and find help and justice. To address the problem the project raises awareness and capacity of local communities, professionals and authorities regarding the ongoing sexual abuse of boys and young men. The project activities are awareness raising, trainings to social workers, police and other professionals, training of trainers, producing information material and campaigning, an outreach programme for support and counselling and peer support groups. The expected results are decreased abuse and risk of marginalization, better access to relevant psychosocial support and safe re-integration in the society for the male victims of exploitation.Beneficiaries are victims of sexual abuse, their families and caregivers, relevant professionals working with children, also other NGOs in Phnom Penh and Siem Riep. The implementing partner is First Step.

title: F.a: Cambodia Changemaker Network (CCN)
description: In Cambodia 65 % of the population is under age of 30 and therefore youth empowerment is an imperative. While youth is dynamic resource, there is little representation of young people in decision-making process. Robust youth participation is perhaps the strongest mechanism to enable their potential contribute to the development of their community. By building capacity among Cambodian youth, Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) is empowering the next generation of leaders and agents of change.Objectives: To enhance space and opportunities for youth to be actively involved in the society and policy making process  To increase knowledge, skills and awareness of youth on human rights, education and peaceExpected Result:  Youth have enhanced knowledge and capacity to constructively engage in advocacy actions Youth have increased opportunity and spaces to express their voices on their concerned issues Strengthened youth organisation and networkingRights-holders/beneficiaries:Cambodia Changemaker Network has identified the core to establish the network in 2014. During 2015 this group has been growing to more than 100 members with diverse background including high school students, university students, monks, disabled, and staff from different NGOs and public sector. Many of them are from Phnom Penh city, and some smaller numbers are from provinces including Kom Pong Spue, Bonteay Meanchey, Kompong Cham, Siem Reap, Battam Bong, Kandal, and Prey Veng. Implementing partner: Khmer Youth Association (KYA) was a hosting partner for Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) in 2015, but for 2016 CNN members have agreed to have FCA as the hosting partner. FCA is able to provide effective administration and other technical support to the network as needed.

title: F.a: Cambodia Changemaker Network
description: 1. Project: 11713 Changemaker Cambodia#2. Project area and Country: Phnom Penh, Kompong Spue and Takeo provinces in Cambodia#3. Project justification: #Of the 15.6 million total population, one in five Cambodians (20.6%) are between the ages of 15 and 24. Two thirds of the population is under 30 years of age. However, youth voices are hardly reflected in the countrys policies and programmes, at local or national levels. The response from the government is still partial, fragmented and politicized. The main barrier towards meaningful participation is a lack of recognition of the youth, caused by an age and knowledge hierarchy within the society. FCA Cambodia has enabled spaces for youth to create positive social change through promoting youth participation and advocacy activities. Changemaker Cambodia Network has been established as a platform where youth are empowered to become future leaders and agents of positive change in their communities.#4. The main objective and expected results:#The main objective of the project is to enable youth (CM members and youth they work with) to participate more actively and openly in their communities. The project aims to improve youths knowledge of education opportunities and their capacities in critical skills, analytical thinking and media readiness. The youth members are reaching out to a wider population in different provinces in Cambodia and their activities include campaigns and awareness raising workshops. Local authority (village and commune chiefs) are engaged in almost all of Changemaker Network activities as strategic partner at their target areas to bridge relationship and to change negative perspective and behavior between younger and older generation so that youths initiatives are recognized and supported. Changemaker Cambodia Network is hosted by FCA and its members independently design, propose and implement their own activities. They are advised and supported by FCA staff members.#5. Right-holders/ beneficiaries: Changemaker Cambodia network - 75 youth members (40 females) mainly living in Phnom Penh city#Duty bearers: Local authority (village and commune chiefs) #6. Implementing partner: FCA

title: Improving Health and Well-Being of Human Rights Defenders and Vulnerable Cambodians
description: As part of the project the Cambodian League for the Promotion and Defense of Human Rights (LICADHO) provides basic healthcare sevrices to human rights defenders and vulnerable Cambodians in Phnom Penh and 13 provinces. The medical team of LICADHO provides eg. medical check ups and other services to victims of human rights abuse human rights defenders and prison inmates and sends medical missions to events with an increased risks for vulnerable people e.g. land dispute related demonstrations protests and community events. As part of the project LICADHO also conducts documentation of medical statistics related to health services to such vulnerable groups. As a result of the project victims of human rights abuses and prison inmates and guards will have improved access to basic health services and treatment and human rights defenders will have access to preventive care. In addition it will result in increased knowledge about violent human rights abuses. In Cambodia the situation of human rights defenders and activists is difficult and human rights abuses occur. The availability of health care services is inequal the health sector is underresources and the prisons exceed their capacity. This project will furhter the access of the most vulnerable people to health services. It will also promote the development of the civil society in Cambodia.

LWD has good experience in implementing integrated development and livelihood projects through rights based empowerment approach. The participation and community mobilisation experiences are the strengths of LWD, which is one of the highly appreciated local NGOs. LWD has a strong expertise in managing development work in a transparent and accountable manner.

The project objectives include:1) Enhanced local good governance through trainings and consultations for Commune Councils, Community based organisations, provincial and district officers as well as support to communities in advocacy initiatives on good governance, human rights, legal regulation etc.2) Improved sustainable partner households' livelihoods in the communities through capacity building on agricultural and entrepreneur skills to farmers, vocational skill trainings to selected farmers as well as support Agricultural Cooperatives' (AC) and Village Banks' (VB).3) Increased resilience of communities in disaster prone areas and promote responsiveness of Commune Committee for Disaster Management (CCDM) in Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA).The key groups are marginalised, poorest and most vulnerable households and people affected by any disasters, economic shock, human rights abuses identified by the government's IDPoor system and dataset. Also those vulnerable households who are not included in the system, due to any reasons: women, children, people with disabilities, elderly, ethnic minorities.Implementing partner: Life with Dignity (LWD)LWD is FCA's long-term and strategic partner in Cambodia. LWD has good experience in implementing integrated development and livelihood projects through rights based empowerment approach. The participation and community mobilisation experiences are the strengths of LWD, which is one of the highly appreciated local NGOs. LWD has a strong expertise in managing development work in a transparent and accountable manner.

title: F.a: ESRP Climate Change adaptive agriculture
description: 1. Project: 11873 Climate change adaptive agriculture project#2. Project area and Country: Pursat province in Cambodia #3. Project justification: #Cambodia is generally regarded as one of the worlds most vulnerable countries to the impacts of climate change and the extreme weather conditions are likely to be exacerbated in the future. Dependency on rain-fed agriculture and limited adaptive capacity make the country even more vulnerable to the impacts of the climate change. The expected long-term impacts will worsen the existing risks Cambodia is already facing, especially flooding. Pursat province is affected both by floods and droughts, which have affected local food production and increased food-insecurity. #4. The main objective and the expected results:#The main objective of the Climate change adaptive agriculture project is to improve the capability of vulnerable youths, children and community members to adapt to the impacts of climate change and enhance resilience to disasters. The project will focus on Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA) to build the capacity in vulnerable communities by educating youth and children in primary schools on DRR and CCA. At the end of the project, vulnerable community members, youths, and school-children will have improved capacity in DRR/CCA and to cope with disaster risks and climate change impacts. Land managed under climate resilience practices and water use efficiency by women and men will increase.#5. Right-holders/ beneficiaries: 3,130 people (school children, youth and community members)#Duty bearers: Government officials working on DRR from provincial and district levels, parents, commune counsellors, school principals, and teachers#6. Implementing partner: Life With Dignity (LWD)

title: Frame Agreement with NGO (Finn Church Aid)
description: Cambodia's 2001 Land Law attempted to limit encroachment into state land (technically about 80% of Cambodia's land area) while providing for legal expansion of smallholder agriculture through the distribution of up to five hectares of state land as 'social land concessions' which would be eligible for title after five years of continuous occupation and use. In 2003, Sub-Decree 19 on Social Land Concessions (SLCs) was enacted which provided for a locally initiated and managed process of planning and implementing SLCs. In late 2005, the State Land Management Sub-Decree provided the legal basis for district and provincial levels of Government to work with communes to identify and officially allocate state lands for SLCs.Land and Advocacy Development Project (LADP) has been prepared to provide capacity building on Alternative Dispute resolution (ADR) Land Rights and Land Registration, Advocacy, Women Rights, and relevant laws to ensure that the people are aware of ADR and the responsibilities of government and other duty-bearers to fulfill, to protect and respect communities' rights. In addition, the capacity of the duty bearers will be strengthened to be able to fulfill their obligations to realise concerned communities' rights. Objectives: To promote democratic participation and human rights at the grassroots level by educating and supporting vulnerable groups, victims of land dispute and local government (Commune Councils) to become more effective at advocating their communities' needs. To ensure the most vulnerable groups are able to access to their agriculture land and control over productive resources and assets for enhancing their livelihood activities. Rights- holders /beneficiaries: Approximately 1 000 households located in 25 villages at selected LWD programme areas in Kampong Speu, Kampong Chhnang, Pursat, Battambang provinces will benefit from the project. The district Cadastral Commission, local authority and LWD staff will benefit from the project through capacity building on Alternative Dispute Resolution. Implementing partner: Life with Dignity (LWD)LWD has been working together with FCA in partnership for over 20 years to improve the livelihoods of the poor and marginalised in rural Cambodia, engaging both rights-holders and duty-bearers. Since 2011, the partners have been implementing a land rights awareness project in Kampong Chhnang and Kampong Speu provinces with the aim at increasing awareness on land rights and land registration of vulnerable households who have received land through Social Land Concessions. Land rights and land registration trainings were also provided to district authority representatives, Commune Councils, village leaders, Advocacy Group and implementing partner staff in collaboration with the Ministry of Land Management, Urban Planning and Construction (MLMUPC).

title: F.a: Land and Livelihood Advocacy Development Project (LLAP)
description: The number of land conflicts has been significantly increased over the last 10 years in Cambodia. However, the 2001 land law was adopted following other supporting mechanisms. The land demarcation done by the relevant authorities and also the youth volunteers (following Directive 01) has not been clear especially in the land conflict areas. Both the citizens and authorities who have been involved in the conflict and conflict resolution found the difficulties in addressing the issues without statistics and lack of information. Moreover, lack of land certificate and overlapping in certificates has put the land demarcation in difficulties.The aim of Land and Livelihood Advocacy Project (LLAP) is to provide capacity building on basic Alternative Dispute resolution (ADR), Family Law, Land Rights and Land Registration, Advocacy, Women Rights, and other relevant laws through trainings, awareness raising, workshops, commune forums, meetings and dialogue. Expected results: people at the target areas are aware of ADR, their rights are fulfilled and dealing with issues is done in a peaceful manner. This will be achieved when community members are aware of the responsibilities of government and duty-bearers [such as District/Khan Cadastral Commissions (DKCC), Commune Councils (CCs), Local Authorities (LAs)] have improved capacity on Alternative Dispute Resolution and land law to fulfill, to protect and respect communities' rights. Thus the capacity of the duty-bearers will be strengthened to be able to fulfill their obligations to realise the rights of the communities. Rights- holders /beneficiaries: At least 31,787 households located in 25 villages at selected LWD programme areas in Kampong Speu, Kampong Chhnang, Pursat, Battambang provinces will benefit from the project. The district Cadastral Commission, local authorities and LWD staff will benefit from the project through capacity building on Alternative Dispute Resolution. Life with Dignity (LWD) has been working together with FCA in partnership for over 20 years to improve the livelihoods of the poor and marginalized in rural Cambodia, engaging both rights-holders and duty-bearers.

title: F.a: Cooperation for women's economic developpment CWED -Phase II
description: 1. Project: 11874 Cooperation for Womens Economic Empowerment (CWED II)#2. Project area and Country: Battambang, Pursat, Kampong Chhnang and Kampong Spue provinces in Cambodia#3. Project justification: #Women are often marginalized in the communities in Cambodia. They have lower educational levels than men, and the culture and conservative traditional norms value women less than men. Gender power imbalances create barriers that prevent women from effectively participating in the development of their communities. In addition to lack of technical skills and support, womens knowledge of their rights remains limited. Cooperatives have proven to be an effective means to poor to pool their resources and enhance access to markets. However, poor women still cannot benefit from the work of the cooperatives because they cannot afford to buy the shares of the cooperatives or have sufficient production to be able to participate in the saving and loan schemes run by the cooperatives.#4. The main objective and expected results:#Successful achievements of Cooperation for Womens Economic Empowerment in Phase I (2015-2017), in introducing a business linkage between cooperatives and private companies, have encouraged women to participate in the cooperatives. CWED II project aims to contribute to womens economic and social empowerment so that women become equal and active participants in the sustainable development of their communities. The vulnerable womens business and income generating opportunities will be enhanced and participation in decision-making increased. The 17 targeted Women Agricultural Cooperatives (WAC) will have appropriate structures, strengthened management and operational capacity. The WACs will have the capacity to provide services to their increased and strengthened membership. The project will also strengthen the ownership and commitment of duty bearer toward WACs. #5. Right-holders/beneficiaries: 9,200 rights-holders at the end of the project (2020). #Duty bearers: The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Provincial Department of Agriculture, Provincial Agriculture Cooperative Promotion Office, District Office of Agriculture, Commune Councils and Village Development Committees. #6. Implementing partner: A consortium with FCA, Life With Dignity (LWF) and Interchurch Cooperation for Development (ICCO)

title: F.a: Cooperation for women's economic developpment CWED
description: 1. Project: 11552 Cooperation for Womens Economic Development (CWED) #2. Project area and Country: Battambang, Pursat, Kampong Chhnang and Kampong Spue provinces in Cambodia# 3. Project justification: #Cooperation for Womens Economic Development (CWED) project, which started in the beginning of 2015, came to an end in 2017. There were some delays in project implementation mainly due to staff turnover. FCAs partner LWD proposed a no-cost extension of 4 months from January to April 2018 to carry out the remaining activities and accomplish the set results.#4. The main objective and expected results:#The project is aiming at womens empowerment, economic development, and building their confidence to make decisions. The project will promote entrepreneurship, continue to support vulnerable women to play an active role to lead and manage Agriculture Cooperatives and establish market linkages through value chain concepts.  The project will continue to build WACs capacity, while further strengthening the coordination with various stakeholders. The main activities include establishing business network and products fair, installing collective smart agriculture demo and learning sites, conducting entrepreneurship and standardize book keeping training, and setting up the operational model for micro and small business groups. Final project evaluation will also be conducted.#5. Right-holders/beneficiaries: At least 2,331 direct beneficiaries (members of 12 WACs in 4 provinces) Indirect beneficiaries are the families of the WAC members and community residents. At least 80% of the direct beneficiaries are women.#Duty bearers: Local authorities and Village Development Committees. #6. Implementing partner: Life With Dignity (LWF)

title: F.a: Land and livelihood advocacy project
description: 1. Project: 11435 Land and Livelihood Advocacy Project (LLAP)#2. Project area and Country: Pursat and Kampong Speu Provinces in Cambodia.#3. Project justification: #Accessing land titles is still a constraint for many people in rural Cambodia. The vulnerable people in the communities often have no land titles, which then results into land conflicts with their neighbours and newcomers as the lands of the poor people are easy targets for powerful people and private companies. When land conflict cases have been brought to the provincial court, the ruling is often against the poor people due to corruption. The majority of community people are illiterate and do not understand the processes to obtain rights to land, besides which they lack information form the relevant authorities on Land Law and Land Registration. In addition, the duty-bearers have poor knowledge and skills on Alternative Disputes Resolution (ADR) and have to send all land conflicts to district and provincial courts for decision-making.#4. The main objective and the expected results:#The main objective of the Land and Livelihood Advocacy Project is to improve the quality of the dispute resolution process and to increase access to justice by the poor in Pursat and Kampong Speu Provinces. The project seeks to provide the commune councils with the necessarily skills to mediate and resolve conflicts related to land and family issues at the local level. It also aims to build the capacity of the district officers to work together with the commune council to solve the land and family conflicts. The project will continue the capacity building on basic Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) started in the previous phase.#At the end of the project, the targeted community members will have increased knowledge and understanding of Land Law and Rights and basic Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) and Family Law. The project will also promote dialogue platform on land conflict resolution for right holders and duty bearers at national level and will carry out case investigation on the reported disputes.#5. Right-holders/ beneficiaries: 4,560 beneficiaries (farmers, youth, and elderly)#Duty bearers: District officials, commune councilors, and village chiefs#6. Implementing partner: Life With Dignity (LWD)

title: F.a: Chab Dai- assisting victims of human trafficking
description: Cambodia is a country of both origin and transit for human trafficking. The relations and trust between the police and communities has historically been weak and not serving the best interest of victims. The project builds the capacity of duty bearers (police and authorities, government and other stakeholders) in providing protection and access to justice to the child victims of human trafficking and abuse. A training curriculum will be designed based on a study of the authorities' knowledge and skills regarding child rights. Training material will be made to address the real needs of the authorities working directly with victims and their families. The training will cover the psycho-social aspects of the work with child victims, as well as appropriate legal procedures and law. Project will also facilitate trainings on Child Rights in communities, including local police and authorities in order to build better relations and trust between the police and communities. The expected results of the project are improved understanding and strengthened practices of child rights, children are protected better from exploitation and victims and their families are protected and have access to justice. A connected network will be formed to facilitate a timely and coordinated child victim care and child protection. Direct beneficiaries are 60 local Police in Prey Veng and Svay Rieng, 210 local community people, community and church leaders. Final beneficiaries are children who are in danger of exploitation and human trafficking. The implementing partner is Chab Dai Coalition.

title: F.a: Cambodia Changemaker Network (CCN)

By building capacity among Cambodian youth, Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) is empowering the next generation of leaders and agents of change.Objectives: To enhance space and opportunities for youth to be actively involved in the society and policy making process  To increase knowledge, skills and awareness of youth on human rights, education and peaceExpected Result:  Youth have enhanced knowledge and capacity to constructively engage in advocacy actions Youth have increased opportunity and spaces to express their voices on their concerned issues Strengthened youth organisation and networkingRights-holders/beneficiaries:Cambodia Changemaker Network has identified the core to establish the network in 2014. During 2015 this group has been growing to more than 100 members with diverse background including high school students, university students, monks, disabled, and staff from different NGOs and public sector. Many of them are from Phnom Penh city, and some smaller numbers are from provinces including Kom Pong Spue, Bonteay Meanchey, Kompong Cham, Siem Reap, Battam Bong, Kandal, and Prey Veng. title: BATTAMBANG MINE CLEARANCE PROJECT
INTEGRATED RURAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECT, BATTAMBANG, CAMBODIA

title: Frame Agreement with NGO (Finn Church Aid)
description: Cambodia's 2001 Land Law attempted to limit encroachment into state land (technically about 80% of Cambodia's land area) while providing for legal expansion of smallholder agriculture through the distribution of up to five hectares of state land as 'social land concessions' which would be eligible for title after five years of continuous occupation and use. In 2003, Sub-Decree 19 on Social Land Concessions (SLCs) was enacted which provided for a locally initiated and managed process of planning and implementing SLCs. In late 2005, the State Land Management Sub-Decree provided the legal basis for district and provincial levels of Government to work with communes to identify and officially allocate state lands for SLCs.Land and Advocacy Development Project (LADP) has been prepared to provide capacity building on Alternative Dispute resolution (ADR) Land Rights and Land Registration, Advocacy, Women Rights, and relevant laws to ensure that the people are aware of ADR and the responsibilities of government and other duty-bearers to fulfill, to protect and respect communities' rights. In addition, the capacity of the duty bearers will be strengthened to be able to fulfill their obligations to realise concerned communities' rights. Objectives: To promote democratic participation and human rights at the grassroots level by educating and supporting vulnerable groups, victims of land dispute and local government (Commune Councils) to become more effective at advocating their communities' needs. To ensure the most vulnerable groups are able to access to their agriculture land and control over productive resources and assets for enhancing their livelihood activities. Implementing partner: Life with Dignity (LWD)LWD has been working together with FCA in partnership for over 20 years to improve the livelihoods of the poor and marginalised in rural Cambodia, engaging both rights-holders and duty-bearers. Land rights and land registration trainings were also provided to district authority representatives, Commune Councils, village leaders, Advocacy Group and implementing partner staff in collaboration with the Ministry of Land Management, Urban Planning and Construction (MLMUPC).

title: F.a: To improve livelihood of income generation of small business establishing, livestock raising and Tuktuk social enterprise.
description: 15 persons with a spinal cord injury in Battambang Cambodia are trained on running their own small business and will receive some start-up capital to start their business of livestock raising, small business e.g. grocery selling or accessible Tuktuk business. title: F.a: Land and Livelihood Advocacy Development Project (LLAP)
description: The number of land conflicts has been significantly increased over the last 10 years in Cambodia. However, the 2001 land law was adopted following other supporting mechanisms. The land demarcation done by the relevant authorities and also the youth volunteers (following Directive 01) has not been clear especially in the land conflict areas. Both the citizens and authorities who have been involved in the conflict and conflict resolution found the difficulties in addressing the issues without statistics and lack of information. Moreover, lack of land certificate and overlapping in certificates has put the land demarcation in difficulties.The aim of Land and Livelihood Advocacy Project (LLAP) is to provide capacity building on basic Alternative Dispute resolution (ADR), Family Law, Land Rights and Land Registration, Advocacy, Women Rights, and other relevant laws through trainings, awareness raising, workshops, commune forums, meetings and dialogue. Expected results: people at the target areas are aware of ADR, their rights are fulfilled and dealing with issues is done in a peaceful manner. This will be achieved when community members are aware of the responsibilities of government and duty-bearers [such as District/Khan Cadastral Commissions (DKCC), Commune Councils (CCs), Local Authorities (LAs)] have improved capacity on Alternative Dispute Resolution and land law to fulfill, to protect and respect communities' rights. Thus the capacity of the duty-bearers will be strengthened to be able to fulfill their obligations to realise the rights of the communities. Rights- holders /beneficiaries: At least 31,787 households located in 25 villages at selected LWD programme areas in Kampong Speu, Kampong Chhnang, Pursat, Battambang provinces will benefit from the project. The district Cadastral Commission, local authorities and LWD staff will benefit from the project through capacity building on Alternative Dispute Resolution. Life with Dignity (LWD) has been working together with FCA in partnership for over 20 years to improve the livelihoods of the poor and marginalized in rural Cambodia, engaging both rights-holders and duty-bearers.

title: F.a: Cambodia Changemaker Network (CCN)
description: In Cambodia 65 % of the population is under age of 30 and therefore youth empowerment is an imperative. While youth is dynamic resource, there is little representation of young people in decision-making process. Robust youth participation is perhaps the strongest mechanism to enable their potential contribute to the development of their community. By building capacity among Cambodian youth, Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) is empowering the next generation of leaders and agents of change.Objectives:Ģ To enhance space and opportunities for youth to be actively involved in the society and policy making process Ģ To increase knowledge, skills and awareness of youth on human rights, education and peaceExpected Result: Ģ Youth have enhanced knowledge and capacity to constructively engage in advocacy actionsĢ Youth have increased opportunity and spaces to express their voices on their concerned issuesĢ Strengthened youth organisation and networkingRights-holders/beneficiaries:Cambodia Changemaker Network has identified the core to establish the network in 2014. During 2015 this group has been growing to more than 100 members with diverse background including high school students, university students, monks, disabled, and staff from different NGOs and public sector. Many of them are from Phnom Penh city, and some smaller numbers are from provinces including Kom Pong Spue, Bonteay Meanchey, Kompong Cham, Siem Reap, Battam Bong, Kandal, and Prey Veng. Implementing partner: Khmer Youth Association (KYA) was a hosting partner for Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) in 2015, but for 2016 CNN members have agreed to have FCA as the hosting partner. FCA is able to provide effective administration and other technical support to the network as needed.

title: F.a: Cooperation for women's economic developpment CWED
description: 1. Project: 11552 Cooperation for Womens Economic Development (CWED) #2. Project area and Country: Battambang, Pursat, Kampong Chhnang and Kampong Spue provinces in Cambodia# 3. Project justification: #Cooperation for Womens Economic Development (CWED) project, which started in the beginning of 2015, came to an end in 2017. There were some delays in project implementation mainly due to staff turnover. FCAs partner LWD proposed a no-cost extension of 4 months from January to April 2018 to carry out the remaining activities and accomplish the set results.#4. The main objective and expected results:#The project is aiming at womens empowerment, economic development, and building their confidence to make decisions. The project will promote entrepreneurship, continue to support vulnerable women to play an active role to lead and manage Agriculture Cooperatives and establish market linkages through value chain concepts.  The project will continue to build WACs capacity, while further strengthening the coordination with various stakeholders. The main activities include establishing business network and products fair, installing collective smart agriculture demo and learning sites, conducting entrepreneurship and standardize book keeping training, and setting up the operational model for micro and small business groups. Final project evaluation will also be conducted.#5. Right-holders/beneficiaries: At least 2,331 direct beneficiaries (members of 12 WACs in 4 provinces) Indirect beneficiaries are the families of the WAC members and community residents. At least 80% of the direct beneficiaries are women.#Duty bearers: Local authorities and Village Development Committees. #6. Implementing partner: Life With Dignity (LWF)

title: F.a: Dream school phase II
description: 1. Project: 11876 Dream School Project Phase II#2. Project area and Country: Battambang province, Cambodia#3. Project justification: #The Dream School project extension builds on the successes and lessons learnt of a pilot phase implemented from July 2016 until December 2017 in Battambang province. Access to quality education is constrained by a number of factors in the four targeted communities. School infrastructure is in need of upgrading, and the schools do not provide a safe or supportive learning environment for the children. Some of the schools have high student-teacher ratios with up to 40-50 children in one classroom, while teachers are not aware of the contents of the curriculum and do not master effective teaching methods, and lack motivation and commitment. Also, community commitment to education and cooperation between parents and schools has been identified as one of the key problems. #4. The main objective and expected results: #The main objective of the project is to contribute to children and adolescents improved learning outcomes and life opportunities. The project aims to enhance the skills and capacity of the 85 targeted teachers, 85 teacher trainers and 4 school directors in school management and teaching. Four targeted schools will have a safer and more supportive learning and teaching environment for all learners and teaching staff. The project will promote the engagement and commitment by parents and the local communities to participate in the development and management of schools and their activities. It will also seek to address the issue of girls dropping out of school early through the student council. #5. Right-holders/ beneficiaries: 1774 (children, teachers, school directors, librarians and school support committees members) #Duty bearers: parents, teachers, school directors, District Office of Education/Provincial Office of Education#6. Implementing partner: Puthi Kumar Organization (PKO)

title: F.a: Cooperation for women's economic developpment CWED -Phase II
description: 1. Project: 11874 Cooperation for Womens Economic Empowerment (CWED II)#2. Project area and Country: Battambang, Pursat, Kampong Chhnang and Kampong Spue provinces in Cambodia#3. Project justification: #Women are often marginalized in the communities in Cambodia. They have lower educational levels than men, and the culture and conservative traditional norms value women less than men. Gender power imbalances create barriers that prevent women from effectively participating in the development of their communities. In addition to lack of technical skills and support, womens knowledge of their rights remains limited. Cooperatives have proven to be an effective means to poor to pool their resources and enhance access to markets. However, poor women still cannot benefit from the work of the cooperatives because they cannot afford to buy the shares of the cooperatives or have sufficient production to be able to participate in the saving and loan schemes run by the cooperatives.#4. The main objective and expected results:#Successful achievements of Cooperation for Womens Economic Empowerment in Phase I (2015-2017), in introducing a business linkage between cooperatives and private companies, have encouraged women to participate in the cooperatives. CWED II project aims to contribute to womens economic and social empowerment so that women become equal and active participants in the sustainable development of their communities. The vulnerable womens business and income generating opportunities will be enhanced and participation in decision-making increased. The 17 targeted Women Agricultural Cooperatives (WAC) will have appropriate structures, strengthened management and operational capacity. The WACs will have the capacity to provide services to their increased and strengthened membership. The project will also strengthen the ownership and commitment of duty bearer toward WACs. #5. Right-holders/beneficiaries: 9,200 rights-holders at the end of the project (2020). #Duty bearers: The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Provincial Department of Agriculture, Provincial Agriculture Cooperative Promotion Office, District Office of Agriculture, Commune Councils and Village Development Committees. #6. Implementing partner: A consortium with FCA, Life With Dignity (LWF) and Interchurch Cooperation for Development (ICCO)

description: 1. Project: 11771 Promoting Women's Entrepreneurship (PWE) 2. Project area and Country: Siem Reap province in Cambodia 3. Project justification: During 2012-16 Women in Action (WIN) project focused on empowering women and girls in Kralanh and Siem Reap districts in view of improved living conditions with strong social networks so that they are able to overcome financial constraints and reduce vulnerability to all forms of violence. Despite the above achievements, the mid-term evaluation found that women's business group members still have limited skills in business management, especially in planning and marketing. 4. The main objective and expected results:The main objective of the PWE project is to empower women in the target area to become economically self-sufficient by promoting girls' access to education and women's entrepreneurship. title: Promoting child rights and work against child labour
description: The project  We protect children do you? - Promoting Child Rights and Protecting Children from the Worst Forms of Child Labour in Cambodia focuses on the prevention of child labor and the protection of children involved in the worst forms of child labor in particular children engaged in domestic work brick factories and the entertainment industry. According to the recent statistics there are 14 million working children in Cambodia. Within the most dangerous forms of labor the working conditions are extremely damaging to health. Thousands of children lack opportunities for education because of being forced to work. This results to a cycle of illiteracy and poverty. In Cambodia the society doesn?t recognize the need to protect children from exploitation and significant gaps do exist in official child protection structures which makes it important for NGOs to contribute in this field.The project opposes child labor exploitation by developing groups and networks in different community sectors to monitor investigate and refer to child rights (CR) violations. Wider audience is reached through activities that disseminate information on CR and on how to correctly respond to violations. The project also aims to contribute to the prevention of CR violations in Cambodia and to the protection and rehabilitation of victims of the violations.The project is located in both rural and urban areas in Phnom Penh and its surroundings and the provinces of Kandal Koh Kong Preah Sihanouk and Siem Reap.The first project phase has been successful in establishing local level Child Protection Groups (PG) especially Child PGs in the target communities. The public awareness and debate about Child Rights and risks of the Child Labour is also increasing. This continuation phase of the project (2014-2015) will be dedicated especially to strengthening the existing Child Protection Groups as part of the local level civil societies. To ensure their continuation as independent actors the number of members in the PGs will be increased child and youth PG members' participation and capacity to advocate with peers strenghtened and networking and links to other local level actors  reinforced. Child and youth participation in local level decision making structures (commune/Sangkat meetings) will also be strenghtened to increase the child and youth perspective in the decision making.

title: Frame Agreement with NGO (Finn Church Aid)
description: Deep-rooted gender inequalities and gender-based violence (GBV) are pervasive in Cambodian society, particularly in areas where poverty is widespread, unemployment is high, and education levels are low. The low levels of literacy and education limit women's options for generating sufficient income for decent living which exposes them and their children to the risk of exploitation and violence. In addition, low family incomes and social attitudes all combine to create numerous barriers to girls attending or remaining in school, causing them to drop out before completing their basic education and thereby increasing their vulnerability. Women and girls also have less voice and thus little influence in decision-making processes in their communities due to prevailing gender stereotypes.The target area of the project is Siem Reap province which is one of the poorest provinces of Cambodia, with a high number of female-headed households, most of whom are poor and under considerable economic and social stress. Project objectives include: Empowered women are able to generate income through group businesses and small enterprises Clusters of savings groups formed into Federations in the target areas to provide support to vulnerable women to curb financial crisis and all forms of violence Girls from poor families living in the target areas are empowered through access to education (scholarships, vocational and life skills training)  Rights-holders /beneficiaries: The most vulnerable women and girls including women from poor families, landless and women recovering from violence, men and boys will also benefit directly and indirectly from saving groups and community awareness, CWCC staff, family members of targeted women, community members, partner NGOs and members of local authorities. title: F.a: Women In Action project (WIN)
description: Deep-rooted gender inequalities and gender-based violence (GBV) are pervasive in Cambodian society, particularly in areas where poverty is widespread, unemployment is high, and education levels are low. The low levels of literacy and education limit women's options for generating sufficient income for decent living which exposes them and their children to the risk of exploitation and violence. In addition, low family incomes and social attitudes all combine to create numerous barriers to girls attending or remaining in school, causing them to drop out before completing their basic education and thereby increasing their vulnerability. Women and girls also have less voice and thus little influence in decision-making processes in their communities due to prevailing gender stereotypes.The target area of the project is Siem Reap province which is one of the poorest provinces of Cambodia, with a high number of female-headed households, most of whom are poor and under considerable economic and social stress. Expected results: 20 saving schemes (saving for change) established with active participation from targeted communities and income generation activities/businesses identified and selected based on the result of the market survey Girls from poor families living in target communities received a scholarship package so they can continue their study at public school Target communities gradually improved understanding of the importance of girl's access to education Youth club established and capacity building provided to become focal group in providing awareness campaigns to community members Rights-holders /beneficiaries: The most vulnerable women and girls including women from poor families, landless and women recovering from violence, men and boys will also benefit directly and indirectly from saving groups and community awareness, CWCC staff, family members of targeted women, community members, partner NGOs and members of local authorities. Implementing partner: The Cambodia Women's Crisis Centre (CWCC) is a local non-governmental organisation with the aim of combatting all forms of violence against women and children. CWCC has extensive experience in responding to the needs of the most vulnerable groups of society through variety of interventions, including social assistance, legal protection, community organising, economic empowerment through skills training and small business loans and promotion of access to secondary education for girls.

title: F.a: Cambodia Changemaker Network (CCN)
description: In Cambodia 65 % of the population is under age of 30 and therefore youth empowerment is an imperative. While youth is dynamic resource, there is little representation of young people in decision-making process. Robust youth participation is perhaps the strongest mechanism to enable their potential contribute to the development of their community. By building capacity among Cambodian youth, Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) is empowering the next generation of leaders and agents of change.Objectives: To enhance space and opportunities for youth to be actively involved in the society and policy making process  To increase knowledge, skills and awareness of youth on human rights, education and peaceExpected Result:  Youth have enhanced knowledge and capacity to constructively engage in advocacy actions Youth have increased opportunity and spaces to express their voices on their concerned issues Strengthened youth organisation and networkingRights-holders/beneficiaries:Cambodia Changemaker Network has identified the core to establish the network in 2014. During 2015 this group has been growing to more than 100 members with diverse background including high school students, university students, monks, disabled, and staff from different NGOs and public sector. Many of them are from Phnom Penh city, and some smaller numbers are from provinces including Kom Pong Spue, Bonteay Meanchey, Kompong Cham, Siem Reap, Battam Bong, Kandal, and Prey Veng. Implementing partner: Khmer Youth Association (KYA) was a hosting partner for Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) in 2015, but for 2016 CNN members have agreed to have FCA as the hosting partner. FCA is able to provide effective administration and other technical support to the network as needed.

title: F.a: Inclusive actions for improving women's social status through skills, employment and economic development (INSWEED)
description: 1. Project: 12052 Inclusive actions for improving women's social status through skills, employment and economic development (INSWEED) 2. Project area and Country: Siem Reap province, Cambodia    3. Project justification: Women have fewer productive employment and decent work opportunities in Cambodia. Major challenges to be addressed include limited access to technical and vocational training that enable them to access job opportunities or promote women entrepreneurship. Furthermore, TVET is not popular among youth due to lack of information, and TVET services are not responding to labour market needs. Many Cambodians, especially youth, migrate abroad to seek for better livelihood. Poverty combined with the lack of information and education makes rural people vulnerable to illegal migration, trafficking and sexual exploitation in the destination countries. The project area is highly affected by migration.4. The main objective and the expected results: The main objective of the project is that adolescent girls and their families in the targeted areas are economically empowered and become more active members in their local communities. This will be accomplished through increased access to relevant and quality TVET services for adolescent girls and youth.The project will also enhance adolescent girls' and women's access to jobs and/or establish micro businesses and improve their vocational and soft skills. The project will work with the parents and local communities to increase their support to girls' education and participation in TVET. Furthermore, FCA will contribute its expertise to enhance the quality of TVET services. 5. Right-holders/ beneficiaries: 250 youth access to skill training or TVET, 15 TVET teachers, 1,600 members of saving groups, and 1,000 community members benefitting from community awareness Duty bearers: Ministries of Labour and Vocational Training (MoLVT), Education Youth and Sport (MoEYS), National Employment Agency (NEA), local authorities at district and commune levels6. Implementing partner: FCA and Cambodian Women's Crisis Center (CWCC) in a consortium

title: F.a: Women In Action project (WIN)
description: Deep-rooted gender inequalities and gender-based violence (GBV) are pervasive in Cambodian society, particularly in areas where poverty is widespread, unemployment is high, and education levels are low. The low levels of literacy and education limit women's options for generating sufficient income for decent living which exposes them and their children to the risk of exploitation and violence. In addition, low family incomes and social attitudes all combine to create numerous barriers to girls attending or remaining in school, causing them to drop out before completing their basic education and thereby increasing their vulnerability. Women and girls also have less voice and thus little influence in decision-making processes in their communities due to prevailing gender stereotypes.  The target area of the project is Siem Reap province which is one of the poorest provinces of Cambodia, with a high number of female-headed households, most of whom are poor and under considerable economic and social stress.   Project objectives include: ē Empowered women are able to generate income through group businesses and small enterprises ē Clusters of savings groups formed into Federations in the target areas to provide support to vulnerable women to curb financial crisis and all forms of violence ē Girls from poor families living in the target areas are empowered through access to education (scholarships, vocational and life skills training)     Rights-holders /beneficiaries:  The most vulnerable women and girls including women from poor families, landless and women recovering from violence, men and boys will also benefit directly and indirectly from saving groups and community awareness, CWCC staff, family members of targeted women, community members, partner NGOs and members of local authorities.   Implementing partner:  The Cambodia Women's Crisis Centre (CWCC) is a recognised, local non-governmental organisation established in 1997 with the aim of combatting all forms of violence against women and children. CWCC endeavours to support and empower the survivors to realise their rights and to lead a dignified life. CWCC has extensive experience in responding to the needs of the most vulnerable groups of society through a wide variety of interventions, including social assistance, legal protection, community organising, economic empowerment through skills training and small business loans, and promotion of access to secondary education for vulnerable girls.

title: F.a: Chab Dai- assisting victims of human trafficking
description: Cambodia is a country of both origin and transit for human trafficking. The relations and trust between the police and communities has historically been weak and not serving the best interest of victims. The project builds the capacity of duty bearers (police and authorities, government and other stakeholders) in providing protection and access to justice to the child victims of human trafficking and abuse. A training curriculum will be designed based on a study of the authorities' knowledge and skills regarding child rights. Training material will be made to address the real needs of the authorities working directly with victims and their families. The training will cover the psycho-social aspects of the work with child victims, as well as appropriate legal procedures and law. Project will also facilitate trainings on Child Rights in communities, including local police and authorities in order to build better relations and trust between the police and communities. The expected results of the project are improved understanding and strengthened practices of child rights, children are protected better from exploitation and victims and their families are protected and have access to justice. A connected network will be formed to facilitate a timely and coordinated child victim care and child protection. Direct beneficiaries are 60 local Police in Prey Veng and Svay Rieng, 210 local community people, community and church leaders. Final beneficiaries are children who are in danger of exploitation and human trafficking. The implementing partner is Chab Dai Coalition.

title: F.a: Cambodia Changemaker Network
description: 1. Project: 11713 Changemaker Cambodia#2. Project area and Country: Phnom Penh, Kompong Spue and Takeo provinces in Cambodia#3. Project justification: #Of the 15.6 million total population, one in five Cambodians (20.6%) are between the ages of 15 and 24. Two thirds of the population is under 30 years of age. However, youth voices are hardly reflected in the countrys policies and programmes, at local or national levels. The response from the government is still partial, fragmented and politicized. The main barrier towards meaningful participation is a lack of recognition of the youth, caused by an age and knowledge hierarchy within the society. FCA Cambodia has enabled spaces for youth to create positive social change through promoting youth participation and advocacy activities. Changemaker Cambodia Network has been established as a platform where youth are empowered to become future leaders and agents of positive change in their communities.#4. The project aims to improve youths knowledge of education opportunities and their capacities in critical skills, analytical thinking and media readiness. The youth members are reaching out to a wider population in different provinces in Cambodia and their activities include campaigns and awareness raising workshops. Local authority (village and commune chiefs) are engaged in almost all of Changemaker Network activities as strategic partner at their target areas to bridge relationship and to change negative perspective and behavior between younger and older generation so that youths initiatives are recognized and supported. Changemaker Cambodia Network is hosted by FCA and its members independently design, propose and implement their own activities. They are advised and supported by FCA staff members.#5. Right-holders/ beneficiaries: Changemaker Cambodia network - 75 youth members (40 females) mainly living in Phnom Penh city#Duty bearers: Local authority (village and commune chiefs) #6. Implementing partner: FCA

description: In Cambodia 65 % of the population is under age of 30 and therefore youth empowerment is an imperative. title: F.a: Land and Livelihood Advocacy Development Project (LLAP)
description: The number of land conflicts has been significantly increased over the last 10 years in Cambodia. However, the 2001 land law was adopted following other supporting mechanisms. The land demarcation done by the relevant authorities and also the youth volunteers (following Directive 01) has not been clear especially in the land conflict areas. Both the citizens and authorities who have been involved in the conflict and conflict resolution found the difficulties in addressing the issues without statistics and lack of information. Moreover, lack of land certificate and overlapping in certificates has put the land demarcation in difficulties.The aim of Land and Livelihood Advocacy Project (LLAP) is to provide capacity building on basic Alternative Dispute resolution (ADR), Family Law, Land Rights and Land Registration, Advocacy, Women Rights, and other relevant laws through trainings, awareness raising, workshops, commune forums, meetings and dialogue. Expected results: people at the target areas are aware of ADR, their rights are fulfilled and dealing with issues is done in a peaceful manner. This will be achieved when community members are aware of the responsibilities of government and duty-bearers [such as District/Khan Cadastral Commissions (DKCC), Commune Councils (CCs), Local Authorities (LAs)] have improved capacity on Alternative Dispute Resolution and land law to fulfill, to protect and respect communities' rights. Thus the capacity of the duty-bearers will be strengthened to be able to fulfill their obligations to realise the rights of the communities. Rights- holders /beneficiaries: At least 31,787 households located in 25 villages at selected LWD programme areas in Kampong Speu, Kampong Chhnang, Pursat, Battambang provinces will benefit from the project. The district Cadastral Commission, local authorities and LWD staff will benefit from the project through capacity building on Alternative Dispute Resolution. Life with Dignity (LWD) has been working together with FCA in partnership for over 20 years to improve the livelihoods of the poor and marginalized in rural Cambodia, engaging both rights-holders and duty-bearers.

title: F.a: Cooperation for women's economic developpment CWED

title: F.a: Cooperation for women's economic developpment CWED -Phase II
description: 1. Project: 11874 Cooperation for Womens Economic Empowerment (CWED II)#2. Project area and Country: Battambang, Pursat, Kampong Chhnang and Kampong Spue provinces in Cambodia#3. Project justification: #Women are often marginalized in the communities in Cambodia. They have lower educational levels than men, and the culture and conservative traditional norms value women less than men. Gender power imbalances create barriers that prevent women from effectively participating in the development of their communities. In addition to lack of technical skills and support, womens knowledge of their rights remains limited. Cooperatives have proven to be an effective means to poor to pool their resources and enhance access to markets. However, poor women still cannot benefit from the work of the cooperatives because they cannot afford to buy the shares of the cooperatives or have sufficient production to be able to participate in the saving and loan schemes run by the cooperatives.#4. The main objective and expected results:#Successful achievements of Cooperation for Womens Economic Empowerment in Phase I (2015-2017), in introducing a business linkage between cooperatives and private companies, have encouraged women to participate in the cooperatives. CWED II project aims to contribute to womens economic and social empowerment so that women become equal and active participants in the sustainable development of their communities. The vulnerable womens business and income generating opportunities will be enhanced and participation in decision-making increased. The 17 targeted Women Agricultural Cooperatives (WAC) will have appropriate structures, strengthened management and operational capacity. The WACs will have the capacity to provide services to their increased and strengthened membership. The project will also strengthen the ownership and commitment of duty bearer toward WACs. #5. Right-holders/beneficiaries: 9,200 rights-holders at the end of the project (2020). #Duty bearers: The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Provincial Department of Agriculture, Provincial Agriculture Cooperative Promotion Office, District Office of Agriculture, Commune Councils and Village Development Committees. #6. Implementing partner: A consortium with FCA, Life With Dignity (LWF) and Interchurch Cooperation for Development (ICCO)

title: F.a: Land and Livelihood Advocacy Development Project (LLAP)
description: The number of land conflicts has been significantly increased over the last 10 years in Cambodia. However, the 2001 land law was adopted following other supporting mechanisms. The land demarcation done by the relevant authorities and also the youth volunteers (following Directive 01) has not been clear especially in the land conflict areas. Moreover, lack of land certificate and overlapping in certificates has put the land demarcation in difficulties.The aim of Land and Livelihood Advocacy Project (LLAP) is to provide capacity building on basic Alternative Dispute resolution (ADR), Family Law, Land Rights and Land Registration, Advocacy, Women Rights, and other relevant laws through trainings, awareness raising, workshops, commune forums, meetings and dialogue. The district Cadastral Commission, local authorities and LWD staff will benefit from the project through capacity building on Alternative Dispute Resolution. Life with Dignity (LWD) has been working together with FCA in partnership for over 20 years to improve the livelihoods of the poor and marginalized in rural Cambodia, engaging both rights-holders and duty-bearers.

title: F.a: Cooperation for women's economic developpment CWED
description: 1. Project: 11552 Cooperation for Womens Economic Development (CWED) #2. Project area and Country: Battambang, Pursat, Kampong Chhnang and Kampong Spue provinces in Cambodia# 3. Project justification: #Cooperation for Womens Economic Development (CWED) project, which started in the beginning of 2015, came to an end in 2017. There were some delays in project implementation mainly due to staff turnover. FCAs partner LWD proposed a no-cost extension of 4 months from January to April 2018 to carry out the remaining activities and accomplish the set results.#4. The main objective and expected results:#The project is aiming at womens empowerment, economic development, and building their confidence to make decisions. title: F.a: Cambodia Changemaker Network
description: 1. Project: 11713 Changemaker Cambodia#2. Project area and Country: Phnom Penh, Kompong Spue and Takeo provinces in Cambodia#3. Project justification: #Of the 15.6 million total population, one in five Cambodians (20.6%) are between the ages of 15 and 24. Two thirds of the population is under 30 years of age. However, youth voices are hardly reflected in the countrys policies and programmes, at local or national levels. The response from the government is still partial, fragmented and politicized. FCA Cambodia has enabled spaces for youth to create positive social change through promoting youth participation and advocacy activities. Changemaker Cambodia Network has been established as a platform where youth are empowered to become future leaders and agents of positive change in their communities.#4. The main objective and expected results:#The main objective of the project is to enable youth (CM members and youth they work with) to participate more actively and openly in their communities. The project aims to improve youths knowledge of education opportunities and their capacities in critical skills, analytical thinking and media readiness. The youth members are reaching out to a wider population in different provinces in Cambodia and their activities include campaigns and awareness raising workshops. Local authority (village and commune chiefs) are engaged in almost all of Changemaker Network activities as strategic partner at their target areas to bridge relationship and to change negative perspective and behavior between younger and older generation so that youths initiatives are recognized and supported. Changemaker Cambodia Network is hosted by FCA and its members independently design, propose and implement their own activities. They are advised and supported by FCA staff members.#5. Right-holders/ beneficiaries: Changemaker Cambodia network - 75 youth members (40 females) mainly living in Phnom Penh city#Duty bearers: Local authority (village and commune chiefs) #6.
