title: F.a: Cooperation for women's economic developpment CWED -Phase II
description: 1. Project: 11874 Cooperation for Womens Economic Empowerment (CWED II)#2. Project area and Country: Battambang, Pursat, Kampong Chhnang and Kampong Spue provinces in Cambodia#3. Project justification: #Women are often marginalized in the communities in Cambodia. They have lower educational levels than men, and the culture and conservative traditional norms value women less than men. Gender power imbalances create barriers that prevent women from effectively participating in the development of their communities. In addition to lack of technical skills and support, womens knowledge of their rights remains limited. Cooperatives have proven to be an effective means to poor to pool their resources and enhance access to markets. However, poor women still cannot benefit from the work of the cooperatives because they cannot afford to buy the shares of the cooperatives or have sufficient production to be able to participate in the saving and loan schemes run by the cooperatives.#4. The main objective and expected results:#Successful achievements of Cooperation for Womens Economic Empowerment in Phase I (2015-2017), in introducing a business linkage between cooperatives and private companies, have encouraged women to participate in the cooperatives. CWED II project aims to contribute to womens economic and social empowerment so that women become equal and active participants in the sustainable development of their communities. The vulnerable womens business and income generating opportunities will be enhanced and participation in decision-making increased. The 17 targeted Women Agricultural Cooperatives (WAC) will have appropriate structures, strengthened management and operational capacity. The WACs will have the capacity to provide services to their increased and strengthened membership. The project will also strengthen the ownership and commitment of duty bearer toward WACs. #5. Right-holders/beneficiaries: 9,200 rights-holders at the end of the project (2020). #Duty bearers: The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Provincial Department of Agriculture, Provincial Agriculture Cooperative Promotion Office, District Office of Agriculture, Commune Councils and Village Development Committees. #6. Implementing partner: A consortium with FCA, Life With Dignity (LWF) and Interchurch Cooperation for Development (ICCO)

title: F.a: Land and livelihood advocacy project
description: 1. Project: 11435 Land and Livelihood Advocacy Project (LLAP)#2. Project area and Country: Pursat and Kampong Speu Provinces in Cambodia.#3. Project justification: #Accessing land titles is still a constraint for many people in rural Cambodia. The vulnerable people in the communities often have no land titles, which then results into land conflicts with their neighbours and newcomers as the lands of the poor people are easy targets for powerful people and private companies. When land conflict cases have been brought to the provincial court, the ruling is often against the poor people due to corruption. The majority of community people are illiterate and do not understand the processes to obtain rights to land, besides which they lack information form the relevant authorities on Land Law and Land Registration. In addition, the duty-bearers have poor knowledge and skills on Alternative Disputes Resolution (ADR) and have to send all land conflicts to district and provincial courts for decision-making.#4. The main objective and the expected results:#The main objective of the Land and Livelihood Advocacy Project is to improve the quality of the dispute resolution process and to increase access to justice by the poor in Pursat and Kampong Speu Provinces. The project seeks to provide the commune councils with the necessarily skills to mediate and resolve conflicts related to land and family issues at the local level. It also aims to build the capacity of the district officers to work together with the commune council to solve the land and family conflicts. The project will continue the capacity building on basic Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) started in the previous phase.#At the end of the project, the targeted community members will have increased knowledge and understanding of Land Law and Rights and basic Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) and Family Law. The project will also promote dialogue platform on land conflict resolution for right holders and duty bearers at national level and will carry out case investigation on the reported disputes.#5. Right-holders/ beneficiaries: 4,560 beneficiaries (farmers, youth, and elderly)#Duty bearers: District officials, commune councilors, and village chiefs#6. Implementing partner: Life With Dignity (LWD)

title: F.a: Cambodia Changemaker Network
description: 1. Project: 11713 Changemaker Cambodia#2. Project area and Country: Phnom Penh, Kompong Spue and Takeo provinces in Cambodia#3. Project justification: #Of the 15.6 million total population, one in five Cambodians (20.6%) are between the ages of 15 and 24. Two thirds of the population is under 30 years of age. However, youth voices are hardly reflected in the countrys policies and programmes, at local or national levels. The response from the government is still partial, fragmented and politicized. The main barrier towards meaningful participation is a lack of recognition of the youth, caused by an age and knowledge hierarchy within the society. FCA Cambodia has enabled spaces for youth to create positive social change through promoting youth participation and advocacy activities. Changemaker Cambodia Network has been established as a platform where youth are empowered to become future leaders and agents of positive change in their communities.#4. The main objective and expected results:#The main objective of the project is to enable youth (CM members and youth they work with) to participate more actively and openly in their communities. The project aims to improve youths knowledge of education opportunities and their capacities in critical skills, analytical thinking and media readiness. The youth members are reaching out to a wider population in different provinces in Cambodia and their activities include campaigns and awareness raising workshops. Local authority (village and commune chiefs) are engaged in almost all of Changemaker Network activities as strategic partner at their target areas to bridge relationship and to change negative perspective and behavior between younger and older generation so that youths initiatives are recognized and supported. Changemaker Cambodia Network is hosted by FCA and its members independently design, propose and implement their own activities. They are advised and supported by FCA staff members.#5. title: F.a: Land and livelihood advocacy project
description: 1. Project: 11435 Land and Livelihood Advocacy Project (LLAP)#2. Project area and Country: Pursat and Kampong Speu Provinces in Cambodia.#3. Project justification: #Accessing land titles is still a constraint for many people in rural Cambodia. The vulnerable people in the communities often have no land titles, which then results into land conflicts with their neighbours and newcomers as the lands of the poor people are easy targets for powerful people and private companies. When land conflict cases have been brought to the provincial court, the ruling is often against the poor people due to corruption. The majority of community people are illiterate and do not understand the processes to obtain rights to land, besides which they lack information form the relevant authorities on Land Law and Land Registration. In addition, the duty-bearers have poor knowledge and skills on Alternative Disputes Resolution (ADR) and have to send all land conflicts to district and provincial courts for decision-making.#4. The main objective and the expected results:#The main objective of the Land and Livelihood Advocacy Project is to improve the quality of the dispute resolution process and to increase access to justice by the poor in Pursat and Kampong Speu Provinces. The project seeks to provide the commune councils with the necessarily skills to mediate and resolve conflicts related to land and family issues at the local level. It also aims to build the capacity of the district officers to work together with the commune council to solve the land and family conflicts. The project will continue the capacity building on basic Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) started in the previous phase.#At the end of the project, the targeted community members will have increased knowledge and understanding of Land Law and Rights and basic Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) and Family Law. The project will also promote dialogue platform on land conflict resolution for right holders and duty bearers at national level and will carry out case investigation on the reported disputes.#5. Right-holders/ beneficiaries: 4,560 beneficiaries (farmers, youth, and elderly)#Duty bearers: District officials, commune councilors, and village chiefs#6. Implementing partner: Life With Dignity (LWD)

title: F.a: Community-based support for children with disabilities
description: The project enhances the rights of children with severe disabilities by training communities and their leaders on disability issues and the rights of persons with disabilities, by supporting community based day centres and schools as well as home based care, in Kampot and Kratie provinces. Children with disabilities in Cambodia and their families often live in poverty. Only 3% of disabled children start school and more than half of them drop out soon. Countryside is almost totally lacking educational and supporting services for severely disabled children and ignorance and discriminating attitudes cause enormous barriers to their wellbeing. Without the support of community, parents and authorities the children don't have possibility to develop their skills physically, socially or educationally. However, the work of the project implementer Komar Pikar Foundation (KPF) has proved that by community based solutions even the severely disabled children and their families can have access to education and supporting services and the discrimination can be reduced. As result of the project the children with severe disabilities are accepted as part of their communities, they have possibility to learn and develop their skills and have better access to e.g. health services. The financial status of the families improves and discrimination is reduced.

title: F.a: Cambodia Changemaker Network (CCN)
description: In Cambodia 65 % of the population is under age of 30 and therefore youth empowerment is an imperative. While youth is dynamic resource, there is little representation of young people in decision-making process. Robust youth participation is perhaps the strongest mechanism to enable their potential contribute to the development of their community. By building capacity among Cambodian youth, Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) is empowering the next generation of leaders and agents of change.Objectives: To enhance space and opportunities for youth to be actively involved in the society and policy making process  To increase knowledge, skills and awareness of youth on human rights, education and peaceExpected Result:  Youth have enhanced knowledge and capacity to constructively engage in advocacy actions Youth have increased opportunity and spaces to express their voices on their concerned issues Strengthened youth organisation and networkingRights-holders/beneficiaries:Cambodia Changemaker Network has identified the core to establish the network in 2014. During 2015 this group has been growing to more than 100 members with diverse background including high school students, university students, monks, disabled, and staff from different NGOs and public sector. Many of them are from Phnom Penh city, and some smaller numbers are from provinces including Kom Pong Spue, Bonteay Meanchey, Kompong Cham, Siem Reap, Battam Bong, Kandal, and Prey Veng. Implementing partner: Khmer Youth Association (KYA) was a hosting partner for Cambodia Changemaker Network (CNN) in 2015, but for 2016 CNN members have agreed to have FCA as the hosting partner. FCA is able to provide effective administration and other technical support to the network as needed.

description: Mother Nature organization, a volunteer movement made up of local indigenous communities, youth activists, and members of civil society, has been successfully opposing the proposed Areng hydroelectric dam, which would seriously damage the unique biodiversity of the Central Cardamom Protected Forest in Koh Kong province, and seriously infringe on the human rights of local indigenous communities. With the strong relationship with members of the local communities and other activist groups, effective one-step-ahead-approach, and through the use of a savvy media campaign, Mother Nature has been able to delay the process and make the Areng Valley a talking point. This will be done through the use of a newly created network, which will concentrate its efforts in punctual, public, and innovative activities / campaigns. Pour les aéroports de Phnom Penh et Siem Reap, les investissements concernent principalement la remise en état et l'extension des pistes. La mise ā niveau des infrastructures aéroportuaires soutiendra le développement du tourisme local, et génčrera des retombées économiques importantes pour le gouvernement et pour les populations locales. L'ouverture de l'aéroport de Sihanoukville permettra aussi de faciliter l'exploitation des ressources énergétiques du Golfe de Siam et de favoriser l'expansion des activités logistiques et portuaires de cette région.

title: Au Cambodge, appui au plan d'investissement de la société concessionnaire de trois aéroports
description: La Société Concessionnaire des Aéroports (SCA) est concessionnaire depuis 1995 de l'aéroport de Phnom Penh et depuis 2001 de celui de Siem Reap au Cambodge. En 2006, la société s'est vue confier la construction et l'exploitation de l'aéroport international de Sihanoukville dans le cadre d'une concession avec l'Etat de 35 ans. SCA est détenue majoritairement par le groupe Vinci et par un groupe malaisien. Le pręt de Proparco contribuera au financement du programme d'investissement des trois aéroports dont SCA est concessionnaire au Cambodge. Les investissements prévus pour l'aéroport de Sihanoukville comprennent principalement la remise en état et l'extension de la piste, ainsi que la construction d'un terminal. Pour les aéroports de Phnom Penh et Siem Reap, les investissements concernent principalement la remise en état et l'extension des pistes. La mise ā niveau des infrastructures aéroportuaires soutiendra le développement du tourisme local, et génčrera des retombées économiques importantes pour le gouvernement et pour les populations locales. L'ouverture de l'aéroport de Sihanoukville permettra aussi de faciliter l'exploitation des ressources énergétiques du Golfe de Siam et de favoriser l'expansion des activités logistiques et portuaires de cette région.

title: Au Cambodge, appui au plan d'investissement de la société concessionnaire de trois aéroports
description: La Société Concessionnaire des Aéroports (SCA) est concessionnaire depuis 1995 de l'aéroport de Phnom Penh et depuis 2001 de celui de Siem Reap au Cambodge. En 2006, la société s'est vue confier la construction et l'exploitation de l'aéroport international de Sihanoukville dans le cadre d'une concession avec l'Etat de 35 ans. SCA est détenue majoritairement par le groupe Vinci et par un groupe malaisien. Le pręt de Proparco contribuera au financement du programme d'investissement des trois aéroports dont SCA est concessionnaire au Cambodge. Les investissements prévus pour l'aéroport de Sihanoukville comprennent principalement la remise en état et l'extension de la piste, ainsi que la construction d'un terminal. Pour les aéroports de Phnom Penh et Siem Reap, les investissements concernent principalement la remise en état et l'extension des pistes. La mise ā niveau des infrastructures aéroportuaires soutiendra le développement du tourisme local, et génčrera des retombées économiques importantes pour le gouvernement et pour les populations locales. L'ouverture de l'aéroport de Sihanoukville permettra aussi de faciliter l'exploitation des ressources énergétiques du Golfe de Siam et de favoriser l'expansion des activités logistiques et portuaires de cette région.

title: Enhance Girl Friendly Schools In Rural District Of Cambodia
description: In Cambodia, the lack of adequate sanitation is one of the biggest obstacles to young and adolescent girls' access to education. In Cambodian schools, female students often have to share a bathroom, mostly unclean, with their male colleagues and have access only to poor quality water. With puberty approaching, it therefore becomes very complicated to be able to manage menstruation with serenity and go to class every day. For boys, girls and boys in pre-pubertal age, the situation is still difficult. Poor sanitation in schools has a major impact on the well-being of students, their health and academic performance. The absence of drinking water, adequate bathing, hygienic education at the height, significantly increase the risk of diarrhea, worm infestations or other intestinal diseases. Thus the project aims to break down the barriers that prevent the most vulnerable Cambodian girls and children from enjoying the right to education. For this purpose adequate infrastructure are built in 7 schools in the province of Kampot and Sihanoukville and in line with the WHO's recommendations, correct hygiene habits are being established before the actual construction of the infrastructure. In this way, the changes created will be positive, sustainable and long-term.

title: Enhance Girl Friendly Schools In Rural District Of Cambodia
description: In Cambodia, the lack of adequate sanitation is one of the biggest obstacles to young and adolescent girls' access to education. In Cambodian schools, female students often have to share a bathroom, mostly unclean, with their male colleagues and have access only to poor quality water. With puberty approaching, it therefore becomes very complicated to be able to manage menstruation with serenity and go to class every day. For boys, girls and boys in pre-pubertal age, the situation is still difficult. Poor sanitation in schools has a major impact on the well-being of students, their health and academic performance. The absence of drinking water, adequate bathing, hygienic education at the height, significantly increase the risk of diarrhea, worm infestations or other intestinal diseases. Thus the project aims to break down the barriers that prevent the most vulnerable Cambodian girls and children from enjoying the right to education. For this purpose adequate infrastructure are built in 7 schools in the province of Kampot and Sihanoukville and in line with the WHO's recommendations, correct hygiene habits are being established before the actual construction of the infrastructure. In this way, the changes created will be positive, sustainable and long-term.

title: UNICEF Social Inclusion and Governance 2018-2021 - UNICEF Social Inclusion and Governance
description: The proposal to Sida concerns core support to the thematic programme Social inclusion and governance, in Cambodia. The Swedish thematic programme support of 29 000 000 SEK covers approximately 40% of the planned program funds during the period. The focus population are vulnerable girls and boys, women and families. The geographical focus is on urban and rural areas of Cambodia in the city region of Phnom Penh and in the provinces Battambang. Kandal, Kratie, Ratanakkiri and Siem Reap.The purpose of the proposed intervention is to address the limited service delivery as an effect of several challenges in the Cambodian context including low spending on social services at sub-national level, limited capacity for delivering social services and weak social accountability mechanism with limited citizen participation in local planning, budgeting and monitoring processes. A key feature of the programme is to support the governments capital and provincial administrations, communes and sangkats to be able to improve the social assistance, and, to roll out the plan to establish a cash transfer system. UNICEF has supported a pilot phase where maximum 90 dollar per month was given to individuals based on specific criteria. The grants were primarily used for food.As the proposal is a thematic program support it is based on (in hierarchic order) the UNICEF country programme for the area, the rolling Work Plan and the proposal to Sida. Therefore, all results planned for in the thematic section will be supported by Sweden. However, UNICEF highlights two in the proposal:Outcome 1: Sub-national administrations (capital and provincial administrations, and communes and sangkats) prioritize children and women in public investment programmes and allocate their resources for social services that aim to improve wellbeing of children and women.Outcome 2: Social protection programmes delivered by sub-national administrations, benefitting the most vulnerable children and women.The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) is a United Nations (UN) program headquartered in New York City that provides humanitarian and developmental assistance to children. It is a member of the United Nations Development Group and has a presence in 190 countries. UNICEF began its work in Cambodia in 1952 and opened its country office in 1973. The agency is guided by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and is specifically named in this Convention as a source of expert assistance and advice. UNICEF's strategy is based on a poverty perspective, but also on overall rights and gender equality.

title: RECOFTC, Partnership for Forestry and Fisheries Community in Cambodia - RECOFTC, Partnership for Forestry and Fisheries (PaFF) (NEW REGIONAL STRATEGY)
description: Partnership for Forestry and Fisheries Community in Cambodia (PaFF) has been conducted in two phases since its inception in 2014. The third phase will be led by RECOFTC in partnership with WWF, NTFP-EP and CEPA. The third phase will continue o empower communities and to improve their resilience by promoting community-based livelihoods, protecting ecosystems and reducing the pressures on the communal natural resource base. The third phase will have a stronger focused on improving local communities  enjoyment of their human rights, building capacity at the grassroots level for participation in democratic processes and promoting the rule of law in relation to access to natural resources.The program will support improvements to the policy environment for natural resource management to promote local organisations to take responsible for and to receive benefit from management of natural resources in their communities. The third phase will also priorities improving the sustainability of the community based organisation. Support will be provided to 77 community based organisations from the previous phases in four provinces (Kampong Thom, Kratie, Stung Treng, Preah Vihear) that, in total, are managing more than 90 000 Ha with a combined membership of almost 40 000 persons.The total program budget i approximately 52 million SEK and is funded jointly with the Swiss development agency SDC. Sida s financial contribution is 36 million SEK. Decision:That Sida shall contribute to  Partnership for Forestry and Fisheries Community in Cambodia  during the period 01 July 2021 till 30 June 2023 with the following agreed sums per year.2021: 15 000 000 SEK2022: 15 000 000 SEK2023: 6 000 000 SEKThat 15 000 000 SEK shall be allocated for this purpose from finance code 104050301 for 2021.That 21 000 000 SEK for coming years for this purpose shall be allocated from the framework for outstanding commitments, with the indicative distribution as Sida s budget above.That Samuel Hurtig, Head of Development Cooperation at the Embassy in Phnom Penh on behalf of Sida shall sign the agreement with RECOFTC principally in accordance with the enclosed draft agreement.
implementing_agencies: RECOFTC/Regional Community Forestry Training Center for Asia and the Pacific

title: SWE-2012-059:Livestock in the City - benefits, risks and regulations
description: The urbanization in developing countries is rapid and the poor rural dwellers moving into cities often bring livestock for food security and livelihood reasons. Production of livestock based food in the city is a good opportunity for them to generate incomes. But, there is an increased risk of transmission of zoonotic diseases from livestock to humans and the manure handling do posses an environmental/sanitary and public health risk as well. Usually, regulations for keeping livestock in cities lag behind in developing economies. In this project, to be performed in Phnom Penh in Cambodia, we combine social and veterinary science to analyse and balance the pros and cons for livestock in the city taking gender dynamics into account. These analyses will be compared with existing regulations and then possible interventions will be presented to the Cambodian stakeholders for consideration.

title: Diakonia secure reporting ICT - Diakonia secure reporting
description: Diakonia has submitted a request to the Embassy for a one-year-extension of the ongoing project Human Rights in the Cyber Age: Safeguarding the message and the messenger (UF2012/68825 PHNO, PLUS ID 51100023), also referred to as the ICT project. In the extension proposal, Diakonia concludes that ICT has proved to be a valuable resource for human rights defenders in Cambodia, and that the four partner organisations in the ICT-project are now integrating ICT into all their core awareness raising activities, civil society mobilizing and evidence based advocacy. New ICT-tools are also being used for cost-effective and safe internal communication.Diakonia also concludes that while the foundations have been established during the two-year-project period, continued efforts are needed to build capacity, increase the pool of activists and audience reach, and explore new ICT tools that can be used in the human rights defense and promotion work. The extension period will be used to consolidate the collaborative work between Diakonia and its current four partners. The partners include three human rights organisations, Community Legal Education Center (CLEC), Cambodian League for Promotion and Defense of Human Rights (LICADHO) and Samakum Theang Tnaot (STT) and one media organization, Cambodian Centre for Independent Media (CCIM). It is expected that the continued support will contribute to make some of the key human rights organisations more efficient and effective in their work. It is also expected to create an environment for more accurate and stringent information collection and transmission. The support provided for the extension period amounts to SEK 2.5 million, which makes the total Swedish financial support to this contribution amount to SEK 9.2 million covering the period from January 2013 to December 2015.

title: Diakonia Human Rights and Democracy Program in Cambodia, 2014-2016 - Diakonia Democracy and Human Rights 2014-2016
description: The Diakonia  Human Rights and Democracy Programme in Cambodia  is based on a five-year-perspective. However, the funding request is based on a three-year-period only, in line with previous discussions between the Embassy and Diakonia to this effect. The total budget for the period 2014-2016 amounts to SEK 36 000 000.The main objective of the programme is to support the growth of a pluralistic and independent civil society that is enabled to promote good governance and democratic participation. The intervention is designed to promote active citizenship through a human rights based approach and a strategy of change that stresses awareness raising, organizing and collective action and advocacy as means to enable the right holders to actively participate in the planning and implementation of initiatives that benefit them and improve their access to rights.To this end, Diakonia will continue to provide financial support (mainly in the form of core-funding) and capacity building to a number of local partner organisations (for 2014, the number is 13). In line with the strategy of change, Diakonia will support the development away from a civil society dominated by professional NGOs and top-down service delivery organisations towards a more pluralistic, more empowering, more representative, more independent, less elitist, more gender equal and more democratically organized civil society.The intervention is built around three broad results areas: 1) Democracy, 2) Gender equality, and 3) Human Rights. Promoting democratic values and defending democratic freedoms where they are at risk constitute key principles of the intervention. Actions relating to freedom of assembly, association and expression are particularly pronounced, along with other initiatives trying to counteract infringements of democratic rights. ICT technology is recognized as a key tool for communication, evidence-based advocacy and data collection as well as a means to organise and form associations.The proposed form of Swedish financing is through a grant, which is deemed appropriate for the type of capacity development support that Diakonia is providing. The intervention will be implemented as a project since there are no programme-based alternatives. Diakonia will channel part of the funds to third parties (i.e. local CSOs). Sweden is currently the only donor. Coordination among donors and other stakeholders however remains relevant in order to share information, good practices and lessons learned and to avoid overlapping activities.

title: Diakonia Human Rights and Democracy 2017-2019
description: In October 2016, Diakonia submitted a project proposal to the embassy concerning support to its programme Human Rights and Democracy in Cambodia for the period 2017-2019. The proposed programme is a continuation of a similar programme that was carried out with Swedish support in 2014-2016 and builds on the experiences and results achieved during this previous phase. In line with the programme for 2014-2016, the contribution aims to support the continued growth and consolidation of an active civil society that can contribute to citizens' participation in democratic processes in Cambodia. Diakonia thus focuses on increasing the capacity of rights holders, but also the duty bearers (authorities at local and national level) are involved in different ways. Under the programme, Diakonia will provide support to 13 local partner organizations working in the areas of human rights, legal aid, freedom of expression, labor rights, media, gender, elections and democracy. The support will mainly be provided in the form of core support to the organizations' own activities, but support to capacity strengthening is also included. The intervention will focus on three broad areas: democracy, gender equality and human rights. At aggregate level, Diakonia's expected results are: (1) actors working for democracy have been strengthened in their interaction with authorities and the public, (2) a positive trend in guaranteeing gender equality in society, in initiatives, in participation, in decision-making forums and in distribution of opportunities, and (3) an increased respect for human rights to enable a secure and safe environment for individual participation in democratic processes in family, work and community. The total budget of the intervention amounts to SEK 44 million for the period 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2019.

title: Can mental health and health care be promoted among young prisoners in Cambodia? An intervention study
description: Research on the health and health care of prisoners in low-income countries is scant. The overall objective of present research collaboration is to improve the mental health of young inmates and to strengthen the health care system within the prisons in Cambodia. This will be done through the development of a collaborative partnership between researchers at the Caritas-Center for Child and Adolescent Mental Health (CCAMH) in Phnom Penh and the unit of Epidemiology and Global Health (EpiGH) at Umeå University. This will be achieved through the combination of five interlinked research and capacity building specific aims: Research aimsTo assess prevalence and pattern of mental health problems and life skills among young prisoners,To evaluate the impact of the Life Skills Education intervention to promote mental health among young prisoners,To develop a plan to strengthen the mental health care system in the selected prisons. Capacity building and collaboration aimsTo identify conceptual and methodological approaches to promote mental health among youth prisoners and the strengthening of mental health care system in prisons,To build individual and institutional capacity in both research institutions in the areas above highlighted.The proposed research collaboration can highlight the health situation of youth inmates, give voice to their needs and create a space of dialogue with prison authorities aiming to improve the mental health and health care in the prisons nationwide.

title: Diakonia Human Rights and Democracy 2017-2019
description: In October 2016, Diakonia submitted a project proposal to the embassy concerning support to its programme Human Rights and Democracy in Cambodia for the period 2017-2019.  The proposed programme is a continuation of a similar programme that was carried out with Swedish support in 2014-2016 and builds on the experiences and results achieved during this previous phase. In line with the programme for 2014-2016, the contribution aims to support the continued growth and consolidation of an active civil society that can contribute to citizens' participation in democratic processes in Cambodia. Diakonia thus focuses on increasing the capacity of rights holders, but also the duty bearers (authorities at local and national level) are involved in different ways.  Under the programme, Diakonia will provide support to 13 local partner organizations working in the areas of human rights, legal aid, freedom of expression, labor rights, media, gender, elections and democracy.  The support will mainly be provided in the form of core support to the organizations' own activities, but support to capacity strengthening is also included. The intervention will focus on three broad areas: democracy, gender equality and human rights. At aggregate level, Diakonia's expected results are: (1) actors working for democracy have been strengthened in their interaction with authorities and the public, (2) a positive trend in guaranteeing gender equality in society, in initiatives, in participation, in decision-making forums and in distribution of opportunities, and (3) an increased respect for human rights to enable a secure and safe environment for individual participation in democratic processes in family, work and community. The total budget of the intervention amounts to SEK 44 million for the period 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2019.

title: UNICEF Social Inclusion and Governance 2018-2021 - UNICEF Social Inclusion and Governance
description: The proposal to Sida concerns core support to the thematic programme Social inclusion and governance, in Cambodia. The Swedish thematic programme support of 29 000 000 SEK covers approximately 40% of the planned program funds during the period. The focus population are vulnerable girls and boys, women and families. The geographical focus is on urban and rural areas of Cambodia in the city region of Phnom Penh and in the provinces Battambang. Kandal, Kratie, Ratanakkiri and Siem Reap.The purpose of the proposed intervention is to address the limited service delivery as an effect of several challenges in the Cambodian context including low spending on social services at sub-national level, limited capacity for delivering social services and weak social accountability mechanism with limited citizen participation in local planning, budgeting and monitoring processes. A key feature of the programme is to support the governments capital and provincial administrations, communes and sangkats to be able to improve the social assistance, and, to roll out the plan to establish a cash transfer system. UNICEF has supported a pilot phase where maximum 90 dollar per month was given to individuals based on specific criteria. The grants were primarily used for food.As the proposal is a thematic program support it is based on (in hierarchic order) the UNICEF country programme for the area, the rolling Work Plan and the proposal to Sida. Therefore, all results planned for in the thematic section will be supported by Sweden. However, UNICEF highlights two in the proposal:Outcome 1: Sub-national administrations (capital and provincial administrations, and communes and sangkats) prioritize children and women in public investment programmes and allocate their resources for social services that aim to improve wellbeing of children and women.Outcome 2: Social protection programmes delivered by sub-national administrations, benefitting the most vulnerable children and women.The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) is a United Nations (UN) program headquartered in New York City that provides humanitarian and developmental assistance to children. It is a member of the United Nations Development Group and has a presence in 190 countries. UNICEF began its work in Cambodia in 1952 and opened its country office in 1973. The agency is guided by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and is specifically named in this Convention as a source of expert assistance and advice. UNICEF's strategy is based on a poverty perspective, but also on overall rights and gender equality.

title: Pilot Research Cooperation with RUPP, Cambodia
description: The Royal University of Phnom Penh (RUPP) in Cambodia has applied to Sida for funding of 78 million SEK to contribute to the programme Enhancement of Research Capacity at RUPP towards Poverty Reduction and Sustainable Development during the period 2019-01-01 until 2022-12-31.This bilateral research cooperation programme aims at building research capacity at RUPP in the areas of natural sciences and bioengineering as well as strengthening the university's information and communications technology (ICT) infrastructure. Furthermore, the programme is expected to strengthen RUPP's administrative and research management capacity including results and financial follow-up. The research cooperation will be set up as a 4-year pilot phase and is expected to result in education of MSc and PhD students, establishment of new and development of existing MSc programmes and development of one PhD programme as well as development of ICT infrastructure for the whole university. The programme will be coordinated by the International Science Programme at Uppsala University (ISP/UU) and the Swedish Program for ICT in Developing Regions at Stockholm University (SPIDER/SU) and carried out in cooperation with Swedish university partners. PhD education will be provided according to the  sandwich model  where Cambodian students are registered at Swedish universities and carry out part of their doctoral training in Sweden. The Swedish university partners will also contribute to teaching at RUPP, development of curricula, education of supervisors and collaborative research projects.The planned maximum contribution for the programme is 79 million SEK out of which approximately 46,8 million SEK will be released to RUPP and approximately 21,2 million SEK to Swedish university partners. Costs for subsistence allowances for Cambodian sandwich PhD students in Sweden will amount to approximately 5,6 million SEK. Approximately 5,2 million SEK will be released to ISP/UU and SPIDER/SU for programme coordination and implementation.The legal relationship between Sida and the partners will be governed by agreements at the following levels:1) A Specific agreement between the government of Sweden represented by Sida and the government of Cambodia represented by RUPP. This agreement regulates the overall budget of the programme and amounts allocated to RUPP, Swedish collaborating universities and Swedish programme coordinating entities. RUPP and the Swedish collaborating universities and programme coordinating entities (see below) report to Sida against this Specific agreement.2) Agreements between Sida and the Swedish programme coordinating entities. title: UNICEF Social Inclusion and Governance 2018-2021 - UNICEF Social Inclusion and Governance
description: The proposal to Sida concerns core support to the thematic programme Social inclusion and governance, in Cambodia. The Swedish thematic programme support of 29 000 000 SEK covers approximately 40% of the planned program funds during the period. The focus population are vulnerable girls and boys, women and families. The geographical focus is on urban and rural areas of Cambodia in the city region of Phnom Penh and in the provinces Battambang. Kandal, Kratie, Ratanakkiri and Siem Reap.The purpose of the proposed intervention is to address the limited service delivery as an effect of several challenges in the Cambodian context including low spending on social services at sub-national level, limited capacity for delivering social services and weak social accountability mechanism with limited citizen participation in local planning, budgeting and monitoring processes. A key feature of the programme is to support the governments capital and provincial administrations, communes and sangkats to be able to improve the social assistance, and, to roll out the plan to establish a cash transfer system. UNICEF has supported a pilot phase where maximum 90 dollar per month was given to individuals based on specific criteria. The grants were primarily used for food.As the proposal is a thematic program support it is based on (in hierarchic order) the UNICEF country programme for the area, the rolling Work Plan and the proposal to Sida. Therefore, all results planned for in the thematic section will be supported by Sweden. However, UNICEF highlights two in the proposal:Outcome 1: Sub-national administrations (capital and provincial administrations, and communes and sangkats) prioritize children and women in public investment programmes and allocate their resources for social services that aim to improve wellbeing of children and women.Outcome 2: Social protection programmes delivered by sub-national administrations, benefitting the most vulnerable children and women.The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) is a United Nations (UN) program headquartered in New York City that provides humanitarian and developmental assistance to children. It is a member of the United Nations Development Group and has a presence in 190 countries. UNICEF began its work in Cambodia in 1952 and opened its country office in 1973. The agency is guided by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and is specifically named in this Convention as a source of expert assistance and advice. UNICEF's strategy is based on a poverty perspective, but also on overall rights and gender equality.

title: Can mental health and health care be promoted among young prisoners in Cambodia? An intervention study
description: Research on the health and health care of prisoners in low-income countries is scant. The overall objective of present research collaboration is to improve the mental health of young inmates and to strengthen the health care system within the prisons in Cambodia. This will be done through the development of a collaborative partnership between researchers at the Caritas-Center for Child and Adolescent Mental Health (CCAMH) in Phnom Penh and the unit of Epidemiology and Global Health (EpiGH) at Umeå University. This will be achieved through the combination of five interlinked research and capacity building specific aims: Research aimsTo assess prevalence and pattern of mental health problems and life skills among young prisoners,To evaluate the impact of the Life Skills Education intervention to promote mental health among young prisoners,To develop a plan to strengthen the mental health care system in the selected prisons. Capacity building and collaboration aimsTo identify conceptual and methodological approaches to promote mental health among youth prisoners and the strengthening of mental health care system in prisons,To build individual and institutional capacity in both research institutions in the areas above highlighted.The proposed research collaboration can highlight the health situation of youth inmates, give voice to their needs and create a space of dialogue with prison authorities aiming to improve the mental health and health care in the prisons nationwide.

title: RWI: Cambodia Human Rights Education and Research Programme 2020-2022
description: The Raoul Wallenberg Institute of Human Rights and Humanitarian Law (RWI) has applied for funding of a sum of SEK 30,000,000 from Sida, represented by the Embassy of Sweden in Phnom Penh, to implement the Cambodia Human Rights Education and Research Programme during the period 2020-2022. The main objective of this programme is to strengthen academic institutions in Cambodia to progressively contribute to the promotion of human rights and gender equality. Through the previous programme phase, RWI has institutionally grown and become a trusted cooperation partner to the Embassy and several academic institutions in Cambodia. With a local office established in Cambodia through a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, RWI is fulfilling the legal requirement under the Cambodian laws. With this legal status, RWI has been able to continue good cooperation and partnership with key relevant academic institutions including the universities in Phnom Penh and in a few other provinces as well as professional training centers. The aim is to build up their human rights educational programs and research fields, which will have a positive impact on human rights and gender equality in Cambodia.

title: Capacity Development Partnership Fund III 2018-2021
description: The Capacity Development Partnership Fund (CDPF) was established in 2011 to support key parts of the Cambodian Education Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports' (MoEYS) strategic plan for capacity development. The first phase of the fund was operating in 2011-2014 and a second phase in 2015-2017. The two first phases were jointly funded by the EU Delegation in Phnom Penh, Unicef and Sweden. The steering committee of the CDPF consists of the State Secretary of the MoEYS, directors of the Ministry's different departments and representatives from the donors. UNICEF together with MoEYS Department of Planning acts as the secretariat of the fund and UNICEF is the fund manager.The overall objective of the CDPF is to enable effective leadership and management of the education sector through systematic capacity development thereby enabling implementation of the strategic plan for the education sector's development. The Policy priorities are: 1. Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all 2. Ensure effective leadership and management of education staff at all levels The sub-objectives the CDPF Phase III aim to contribute: 1. To strengthen MoEYS capacity in policy formulation, planning, financing and management of reforms for improved sector performance. 2. To strengthen capacities at provincial and district levels to plan, manage and monitor education service delivery. 3. To strengthen school leadership and capacity in relation to planning and management in order to increase participation and learning.

title: Pilot Research Cooperation with RUPP, Cambodia
description: The Royal University of Phnom Penh (RUPP) in Cambodia has applied to Sida for funding of 78 million SEK to contribute to the programme Enhancement of Research Capacity at RUPP towards Poverty Reduction and Sustainable Development during the period 2019-01-01 until 2022-12-31.This bilateral research cooperation programme aims at building research capacity at RUPP in the areas of natural sciences and bioengineering as well as strengthening the university's information and communications technology (ICT) infrastructure. Furthermore, the programme is expected to strengthen RUPP's administrative and research management capacity including results and financial follow-up. The research cooperation will be set up as a 4-year pilot phase and is expected to result in education of MSc and PhD students, establishment of new and development of existing MSc programmes and development of one PhD programme as well as development of ICT infrastructure for the whole university. The programme will be coordinated by the International Science Programme at Uppsala University (ISP/UU) and the Swedish Program for ICT in Developing Regions at Stockholm University (SPIDER/SU) and carried out in cooperation with Swedish university partners. PhD education will be provided according to the sandwich model where Cambodian students are registered at Swedish universities and carry out part of their doctoral training in Sweden. The Swedish university partners will also contribute to teaching at RUPP, development of curricula, education of supervisors and collaborative research projects.The planned maximum contribution for the programme is 79 million SEK out of which approximately 46,8 million SEK will be released to RUPP and approximately 21,2 million SEK to Swedish university partners. Costs for subsistence allowances for Cambodian sandwich PhD students in Sweden will amount to approximately 5,6 million SEK. Approximately 5,2 million SEK will be released to ISP/UU and SPIDER/SU for programme coordination and implementation.

description: Partnership for Forestry and Fisheries Community in Cambodia (PaFF) has been conducted in two phases since its inception in 2014. title: Diakonia contribution agreement 2021-2025 (CSO strategy) - Diakonia (CSO strategy) 2021-2025
description: Diakonia is a non-profit development organization with work grounded in Christian values. Diakonia s application entitled Changing contexts, supporting change, transforming societies, was received by Sida in October 2020. Below the application is referred to as the CSO-program. The application seeks continued cooperation with Sida for the years 2021-2025 under the CSO-strategy. The total budget for the CSO-program amounts to approximately MSEK 899. The grant applied for from Sida amounts to MSEK 815. The CSO program will be implemented through 24 country programs and about 160 local partners across Africa, Asia, the Middle East/North Africa and Latin America, as well as through a global program. Diakonia s partners constitute religious and non-religious networks and civil society organizations, human rights defenders, coalitions and alliances. In real terms these are women s organizations, groups representing indigenous peoples, movements for people with functional variations and youth movements. Diakonia will continue to work with a focus on democracy, human rights and gender equality. Three organizational transformations are planned. The first of the three transformations is to depart all work from contextual opportunities/challenges, processes and their new theory of change. This change is a departure from previous thematically steered programs. The move, according to Diakonia, will enable increased flexibility in how they can respond to changing developments in the contexts where they work. The second organizational transformation is that the organization will work on the basis of feminist principles. According to Diakonia, this shift introduces a political dimension to the work on equality, which in turn strengthens their continued work in this area and the ambition to achieve gender equality. The third transformation is to broaden the basis for collaborations and enter into new types of collaborations, for example with new actors for change. An increased focus on Diakonia as a learning organization and an increased focus on aid effectiveness, where core support will be a point of departure for support, are reinforcements that are planned in the business. There shall also be a clearer link between core support and capacity building, a greater focus on innovation and on the development of partners  skills.

title: Diakonia Human Rights and Democracy 2017-2019
description: In October 2016, Diakonia submitted a project proposal to the embassy concerning support to its programme Human Rights and Democracy in Cambodia for the period 2017-2019.  The proposed programme is a continuation of a similar programme that was carried out with Swedish support in 2014-2016 and builds on the experiences and results achieved during this previous phase. In line with the programme for 2014-2016, the contribution aims to support the continued growth and consolidation of an active civil society that can contribute to citizens' participation in democratic processes in Cambodia. Diakonia thus focuses on increasing the capacity of rights holders, but also the duty bearers (authorities at local and national level) are involved in different ways.  Under the programme, Diakonia will provide support to 13 local partner organizations working in the areas of human rights, legal aid, freedom of expression, labor rights, media, gender, elections and democracy.  The support will mainly be provided in the form of core support to the organizations  own activities, but support to capacity strengthening is also included. The intervention will focus on three broad areas: democracy, gender equality and human rights. At aggregate level, Diakonia's expected results are: (1) actors working for democracy have been strengthened in their interaction with authorities and the public, (2) a positive trend in guaranteeing gender equality in society, in initiatives, in participation, in decision-making forums and in distribution of opportunities, and (3) an increased respect for human rights to enable a secure and safe environment for individual participation in democratic processes in family, work and community. The total budget of the intervention amounts to SEK 44 million for the period 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2019.

The application seeks continued cooperation with Sida for the years 2021-2025 under the CSO-strategy. The total budget for the CSO-program amounts to approximately MSEK 899. The grant applied for from Sida amounts to MSEK 815. The CSO program will be implemented through 24 country programs and about 160 local partners across Africa, Asia, the Middle East/North Africa and Latin America, as well as through a global program. Diakonia s partners constitute religious and non-religious networks and civil society organizations, human rights defenders, coalitions and alliances. In real terms these are women s organizations, groups representing indigenous peoples, movements for people with functional variations and youth movements. Diakonia will continue to work with a focus on democracy, human rights and gender equality. Three organizational transformations are planned. The first of the three transformations is to depart all work from contextual opportunities/challenges, processes and their new theory of change. This change is a departure from previous thematically steered programs. The move, according to Diakonia, will enable increased flexibility in how they can respond to changing developments in the contexts where they work. The second organizational transformation is that the organization will work on the basis of feminist principles. According to Diakonia, this shift introduces a political dimension to the work on equality, which in turn strengthens their continued work in this area and the ambition to achieve gender equality. The third transformation is to broaden the basis for collaborations and enter into new types of collaborations, for example with new actors for change. An increased focus on Diakonia as a learning organization and an increased focus on aid effectiveness, where core support will be a point of departure for support, are reinforcements that are planned in the business. There shall also be a clearer link between core support and capacity building, a greater focus on innovation and on the development of partners  skills.

title: Pilot Research Cooperation with RUPP, Cambodia
description: The Royal University of Phnom Penh (RUPP) in Cambodia has applied to Sida for funding of 78 million SEK to contribute to the programme Enhancement of Research Capacity at RUPP towards Poverty Reduction and Sustainable Development during the period 2019-01-01 until 2022-12-31.This bilateral research cooperation programme aims at building research capacity at RUPP in the areas of natural sciences and bioengineering as well as strengthening the university's information and communications technology (ICT) infrastructure. Furthermore, the programme is expected to strengthen RUPP s administrative and research management capacity including results and financial follow-up. The research cooperation will be set up as a 4-year pilot phase and is expected to result in education of MSc and PhD students, establishment of new and development of existing MSc programmes and development of one PhD programme as well as development of ICT infrastructure for the whole university. The programme will be coordinated by the International Science Programme at Uppsala University (ISP/UU) and the Swedish Program for ICT in Developing Regions at Stockholm University (SPIDER/SU) and carried out in cooperation with Swedish university partners. PhD education will be provided according to the sandwich model where Cambodian students are registered at Swedish universities and carry out part of their doctoral training in Sweden. The Swedish university partners will also contribute to teaching at RUPP, development of curricula, education of supervisors and collaborative research projects.The planned maximum contribution for the programme is 79 million SEK out of which approximately 46,8 million SEK will be released to RUPP and approximately 21,2 million SEK to Swedish university partners. Costs for subsistence allowances for Cambodian sandwich PhD students in Sweden will amount to approximately 5,6 million SEK. Approximately 5,2 million SEK will be released to ISP/UU and SPIDER/SU for programme coordination and implementation.

title: RWI: Cambodia Human Rights Education and Research Programme 2020-2022 - RWI: Cambodia Human Rights Education and Research Programme 2021
description: The main objective of this programme is to strengthen academic institutions in Cambodia to progressively contribute to the promotion of human rights and gender equality. Through the previous programme phase, RWI has institutionally grown and become a trusted cooperation partner to the Embassy and several academic institutions in Cambodia. With a local office established in Cambodia through a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, RWI is fulfilling the legal requirement under the Cambodian laws. With this legal status, RWI has been able to continue good cooperation and partnership with key relevant academic institutions including the universities in Phnom Penh and in a few other provinces as well as professional training centers. The aim is to build up their human rights educational programs and research fields, which will have a positive impact on human rights and gender equality in Cambodia.

title: EU/PAT II 2021-2022: Parliamentary Centre for Asia, PCAsia, Cambodia - Parliamentary Centre for Asia 2021-2022, Sida financing
description: This initiative concerns support through the newly established Cambodian NGO Parliamentary Center for Asia, PCAsia, to continue to develop the capacity of the Cambodian Parliament and its support functions through training and research. The proposed support is a continuation of previous support through the Cambodian NGO Parliamentary Institute of Cambodia, PIC, which in 2021 set up and will now move all its operations into PCAsia.The aim is to contribute to the improved work of the parliaments that are part of PCAsia s regional area: Cambodia, Myanmar and Lao PDR, by strengthening the capacity of administrative and investigative functions within the parliament, and by increasing the exchange of experience and knowledge between the parliaments. in the region. The PAT programme is designed to complement the EU sector budget support for Cambodia s reform of the public financial management system (OFS). PAT supports the enabling environment for the implementation of the Public Financial Management Reform Programme (PFMRP) in Cambodia focusing on good governance with improved accountability and transparency in the use of public funds.

title: UNICEF Social Inclusion and Governance 2018-2021 - UNICEF Social Inclusion and Governance
description: The proposal to Sida concerns core support to the thematic programme Social inclusion and governance, in Cambodia. The Swedish thematic programme support of 29 000 000 SEK covers approximately 40% of the planned program funds during the period. The focus population are vulnerable girls and boys, women and families. The geographical focus is on urban and rural areas of Cambodia in the city region of Phnom Penh and in the provinces Battambang. Kandal, Kratie, Ratanakkiri and Siem Reap.The purpose of the proposed intervention is to address the limited service delivery as an effect of several challenges in the Cambodian context including low spending on social services at sub-national level, limited capacity for delivering social services and weak social accountability mechanism with limited citizen participation in local planning, budgeting and monitoring processes. A key feature of the programme is to support the governments capital and provincial administrations, communes and sangkats to be able to improve the social assistance, and, to roll out the plan to establish a cash transfer system. UNICEF has supported a pilot phase where maximum 90 dollar per month was given to individuals based on specific criteria. The grants were primarily used for food.As the proposal is a thematic program support it is based on (in hierarchic order) the UNICEF country programme for the area, the rolling Work Plan and the proposal to Sida. Therefore, all results planned for in the thematic section will be supported by Sweden. However, UNICEF highlights two in the proposal:Outcome 1: Sub-national administrations (capital and provincial administrations, and communes and sangkats) prioritize children and women in public investment programmes and allocate their resources for social services that aim to improve wellbeing of children and women.Outcome 2: Social protection programmes delivered by sub-national administrations, benefitting the most vulnerable children and women.The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) is a United Nations (UN) program headquartered in New York City that provides humanitarian and developmental assistance to children. It is a member of the United Nations Development Group and has a presence in 190 countries. UNICEF began its work in Cambodia in 1952 and opened its country office in 1973. The agency is guided by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and is specifically named in this Convention as a source of expert assistance and advice. UNICEF's strategy is based on a poverty perspective, but also on overall rights and gender equality.

title: Career guidance - Swedish Public Employment Service - Finn Church Aid - Swedish Public Employment Service - Career guidance
description: The proposed project,  Career Guidance and Counselling in Secondary Schools - the Bridge to Employment  is a joint venture by the Swedish National Employment Service, Finn Church Aid, the Cambodian Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports and the National Employment Agency. The aim is to provide youth with better understanding of the labour market and which educational pathways could lead to the desired jobs, and to enhance sustainable career development skills of Cambodian youth. This will be done by establishing quality career guidance and counselling (CGC) services in three target provinces' secondary schools and in Mobile Job-Centres or Job-Centres with the goal of expanding the system nationwide at a later stage. The project structure and plan is based on lessons learned from earlier project phases implemented by the project partners.The project will institutionalise supportive processes and structures, e.g. by producing a CGC policy and by introducing Career Counsellor training as a part of teacher training in an existing teacher training institute. The project will give technical assistance for capacity building of governmental authorities in NEA and MoEYS to ensure quality CGC service provision. The project will also produce evidence-based information for the Royal Government of Cambodia on the most effective and appropriate model of CGC service delivery. This will entail expanding existing CGC services within and from Battambang province to two additional provinces to gain experience and collect data for deeper analysis. New Career Counsellors will be trained during the project implementation and supported in their work on school level.One of the main elements of the project is to create closer collaboration for CGC service provision between the formal education sector and the labour market, not with the aim to recruit students to work life too early, but to enhance the awareness of available and relevant study paths and improve youth's soft skills, leading to meaningful sources of livelihoods in later life. For Cambodia's economy to continue growing it needs motivated young professionals, who have the right kind of skills and education. With aligned CGC services guiding students in schools and after graduation this gap can be narrowed.The project will combine local knowledge and contextual requirements with know-how from Finland and Sweden, through fruitful collaboration combining different governmental and non-governmental actors as project partners.

title: PREPARATION RATANAKIRI
UNICEF Social Inclusion and Governance 2018-2021 - UNICEF Social Inclusion and Governance
description: The proposal to Sida concerns core support to the thematic programme Social inclusion and governance, in Cambodia. The Swedish thematic programme support of 29 000 000 SEK covers approximately 40% of the planned program funds during the period. The focus population are vulnerable girls and boys, women and families. The geographical focus is on urban and rural areas of Cambodia in the city region of Phnom Penh and in the provinces Battambang. Kandal, Kratie, Ratanakkiri and Siem Reap.The purpose of the proposed intervention is to address the limited service delivery as an effect of several challenges in the Cambodian context including low spending on social services at sub-national level, limited capacity for delivering social services and weak social accountability mechanism with limited citizen participation in local planning, budgeting and monitoring processes. A key feature of the programme is to support the governments capital and provincial administrations, communes and sangkats to be able to improve the social assistance, and, to roll out the plan to establish a cash transfer system. UNICEF has supported a pilot phase where maximum 90 dollar per month was given to individuals based on specific criteria. The grants were primarily used for food.As the proposal is a thematic program support it is based on (in hierarchic order) the UNICEF country programme for the area, the rolling Work Plan and the proposal to Sida. Therefore, all results planned for in the thematic section will be supported by Sweden. However, UNICEF highlights two in the proposal:Outcome 1: Sub-national administrations (capital and provincial administrations, and communes and sangkats) prioritize children and women in public investment programmes and allocate their resources for social services that aim to improve wellbeing of children and women.Outcome 2: Social protection programmes delivered by sub-national administrations, benefitting the most vulnerable children and women.The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) is a United Nations (UN) program headquartered in New York City that provides humanitarian and developmental assistance to children. It is a member of the United Nations Development Group and has a presence in 190 countries. UNICEF began its work in Cambodia in 1952 and opened its country office in 1973. The agency is guided by the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and is specifically named in this Convention as a source of expert assistance and advice. UNICEF's strategy is based on a poverty perspective, but also on overall rights and gender equality.

title: RECOFTC, Partnership for Forestry and Fisheries Community in Cambodia - RECOFTC, Partnership for Forestry and Fisheries (PaFF)
description: Partnership for Forestry and Fisheries Community in Cambodia (PaFF) has been conducted in two phases since its inception in 2014. The third phase will be led by RECOFTC in partnership with WWF, NTFP-EP and CEPA. The third phase will continue o empower communities and to improve their resilience by promoting community-based livelihoods, protecting ecosystems and reducing the pressures on the communal natural resource base. The third phase will have a stronger focused on improving local communities  enjoyment of their human rights, building capacity at the grassroots level for participation in democratic processes and promoting the rule of law in relation to access to natural resources.The program will support improvements to the policy environment for natural resource management to promote local organisations to take responsible for and to receive benefit from management of natural resources in their communities. The third phase will also priorities improving the sustainability of the community based organisation. Support will be provided to 77 community based organisations from the previous phases in four provinces (Kampong Thom, Kratie, Stung Treng, Preah Vihear) that, in total, are managing more than 90 000 Ha with a combined membership of almost 40 000 persons.The total program budget i approximately 52 million SEK and is funded jointly with the Swiss development agency SDC. Sida s financial contribution is 36 million SEK. Decision:That Sida shall contribute to  Partnership for Forestry and Fisheries Community in Cambodia  during the period 01 July 2021 till 30 June 2023 with the following agreed sums per year.2021: 15 000 000 SEK2022: 15 000 000 SEK2023: 6 000 000 SEKThat 15 000 000 SEK shall be allocated for this purpose from finance code 104050301 for 2021.That 21 000 000 SEK for coming years for this purpose shall be allocated from the framework for outstanding commitments, with the indicative distribution as Sida s budget above.That Samuel Hurtig, Head of Development Cooperation at the Embassy in Phnom Penh on behalf of Sida shall sign the agreement with RECOFTC principally in accordance with the enclosed draft agreement.
implementing_agencies: RECOFTC/Regional Community Forestry Training Center for Asia and the Pacific

title: Kantha Bopha Hospital
description: Dr. Beat Richner, a well known Swiss pediatric doctor, has been managing since 1991 pediatric hospitals in Cambodia on the invitation of the Government of Cambodia. Currently hospitals are located in Phnom Penh and Siem Reap, consisting of several sites (known as Kantha Bopha Hospitals I to V). In 2008, 34.55 millions CHF were raised to cover the costs of the hospitals coming mainly from private donations (about 86.2%), from the Cambodian Government (about 5.2%) and from the Swiss Government (through SDC, about 8.6%, or 3 millions CHF/year). It is estimated that about 80% of all hospital pediatric care in the country is provided by Kantha Bopha. The medical service is free of charge and of high standards. About 2000 staff members are employed among which only two are international. SDC has the Kantha Bopha Foundation, based in Zurich as its interlocutor.  SDC has been supporting the Kantha Bopha since 1994. 5 external evaluations were carried out in 1995, 1997, 2001, 2003 and 2006. Additionally a self assessment was done in 2007. In 2009, SDC came to the conclusion that a new external evaluation would bring very limited new elements, as the project has not changed much in the last 5 years. It was considered more important to check how the numerous recommendations made between 1995 and 2006 have been implemented. Therefore, during the summer 2009, a SDC staff member in charge of quality assurance reviewed all recommendations made so fare and updated accordingly the list of topics to be regularly discussed between SDC and the Kantha Bopha Foundation during its annual meeting.  SDC and the Kantha Bopha Foundation have a yearly dialogue to discuss critical issues, such as: A long term vision including the financial and institutional sustainability as well as a succession plan of Dr. Richner and diversification of incomes. The interaction and gradual integration of Kantha Bopha in the Cambodian Health system A more strategic planning and reporting of the foundation (to reach SDC standards).  Around 2003, the dialogue between SDC and Kantha Bopha (Dr. Richner) was difficult and criticism were made through (interviews in) the media. This situation has changed since 1) SDC has the Foundation and no longer Dr. Richer as an interlocutor and 2) SDC has formalized a regular dialogue with a list of topics for discussion that focus no longer on medical issues but on institutional and financial sustainability.  This project is highly supported by the Swiss public (the fundraising reaches about 25 millions CHF/yr in Switzerland through private donors), is well known and regularly covered by the Swiss media, does a praised professional medical work with clearly identified impact for Cambodia. Development aspects are not sufficiently taken into consideration and long term perspectives are clearly of concern to SDC (heavy dependence on the person of Dr. Richner, parallel structure from the Ministry of Health). SDC discuss all critical points yearly with the Kantha
funding_agencies: Swiss Agency for Development and Co-operation

description: Dr. Beat Richner, a well known Swiss pediatric doctor, has been managing since 1991 pediatric hospitals in Cambodia on the invitation of the Government of Cambodia. Currently hospitals are located in Phnom Penh and Siem Reap, consisting of several sites (known as Kantha Bopha Hospitals I to V). In 2008, 34.55 millions CHF were raised to cover the costs of the hospitals coming mainly from private donations (about 86.2%), from the Cambodian Government (about 5.2%) and from the Swiss Government (through SDC, about 8.6%, or 3 millions CHF/year). It is estimated that about 80% of all hospital pediatric care in the country is provided by Kantha Bopha. The medical service is free of charge and of high standards. About 2000 staff members are employed among which only two are international. SDC has the Kantha Bopha Foundation, based in Zurich as its interlocutor.  SDC has been supporting the Kantha Bopha since 1994. 5 external evaluations were carried out in 1995, 1997, 2001, 2003 and 2006. Additionally a self assessment was done in 2007. In 2009, SDC came to the conclusion that a new external evaluation would bring very limited new elements, as the project has not changed much in the last 5 years. It was considered more important to check how the numerous recommendations made between 1995 and 2006 have been implemented. Therefore, during the summer 2009, a SDC staff member in charge of quality assurance reviewed all recommendations made so fare and updated accordingly the list of topics to be regularly discussed between SDC and the Kantha Bopha Foundation during its annual meeting.  SDC and the Kantha Bopha Foundation have a yearly dialogue to discuss critical issues, such as: A long term vision including the financial and institutional sustainability as well as a succession plan of Dr. Richner and diversification of incomes. The interaction and gradual integration of Kantha Bopha in the Cambodian Health system A more strategic planning and reporting of the foundation (to reach SDC standards).  Around 2003, the dialogue between SDC and Kantha Bopha (Dr. Richner) was difficult and criticism were made through (interviews in) the media. This situation has changed since 1) SDC has the Foundation and no longer Dr. Richer as an interlocutor and 2) SDC has formalized a regular dialogue with a list of topics for discussion that focus no longer on medical issues but on institutional and financial sustainability.  This project is highly supported by the Swiss public (the fundraising reaches about 25 millions CHF/yr in Switzerland through private donors), is well known and regularly covered by the Swiss media, does a praised professional medical work with clearly identified impact for Cambodia. Development aspects are not sufficiently taken into consideration and long term perspectives are clearly of concern to SDC (heavy dependence on the person of Dr. Richner, parallel structure from the Ministry of Health). SDC discuss all critical points yearly with the Kantha

title: Elephant conservation and capacity-building in Keo Seima Wildlife Sanctuary, Cambodia: Year 9.
description: The goal of this project is to improve the protection and conservation status of Asian elephants in Keo Seima Wildlife Sanctuary, Cambodia. The main objectives of this project are to improve anti-snare capacity through applied research and a collection incentive scheme, protect elephants and habitat through targeted law enforcement and anti-snare patrols, and reduce human-elephant conflict (HEC) through implementation of a community-funded insurance scheme. Project activities include: 1) conduct anti-snare efficacy research to identify maximum return-on-investment strategies, 2) improve and re-implement snare collection incentives for anti-snare teams, 3) use remote sensing to detect forest loss and encroachment into high-priority elephant areas and inform patrol planning, 4) conduct law enforcement patrols in high priority areas, 5) review, compile, and collect data to inform design of insurance scheme, 6) conduct feasibility assessment of community-funded insurance scheme in Andong Kralong village, and 7) build capacity of Andong Kralong community to implement insurance scheme.

The Wildlife Sanctuary Support Program works to improve biodiversity conservation and ecosystem health, increases sustainable economic opportunities, and strengthens landscape governance in two wildlife sanctuaries in Mondulkiri province. The activity builds the capacity of local communities and coordinates with Royal Government of Cambodia technical officers to better manage natural resources, supports the analyses and implementation of spatial plans to balance economic development while maintaining the ecological sanctuary's integrity, and, promotes alternative livelihood opportunities to reduce the dependence on the timber and non-timber forest products.
