title: Long-term conservation of Yellow-cheeked crested gibbon through direct law enforcement and community engagement in southern Mondulkiri, Cambodia
description: The purpose of this project is to have well-managed forest landscape that supports increasing wildlife populations, especially gibbons, and improving livelihoods for the people who currently live there. The following objectives and associated activities will be accomplished: (1) Protect gibbons by maintaining extensive law enforcement activities, by (a) continuing proactive law enforcement activities to protect sensitive gibbon habitat, and (b) refining the use of remote sensing and the SMART (Spatial Monitoring and Reporting Tool) software to inform adaptive management, (2) Expand and strengthen community engagement in, and support of, gibbon conservation, by (a) continued capacity building for tourism development and improved community engagement, and (b) further refinement and implementation of robust monitoring of the gibbon populations in the ecotourism area.

title: Cambodia Genocide Research and Education Activity
description: The goal of the Cambodia Genocide Research and Education activity is to conduct researches on history of the Khmer Rouge, train pre-service teacher trainees on genocide education methodology, and raise awareness of the general public on atrocity crimes of the Khmer Rouge and other mass atrocities around the world. The activity will conduct research and outreach activities at the Anlong Veng Peace Center and will also focus on women's rights training in Anlong Veng, located in the Khmer Rouge's last stronghold along the Thai border. Further, the activity will conduct comprehensive research into the Chinese role during the Khmer Rouge.

title: Cambodia Rural Sanitation Development Impact Bond Activity
description: A groundbreaking initiative to bring safe sanitation to some of the poorest and most vulnerable households in Cambodia launches today. The Cambodia Rural Sanitation DIB is the worlds first Development Impact Bond for sanitation and aims to eradicate the high rates of open defecation in the country and accelerate the Cambodian governments efforts to reach universal sanitation. The DIB aims to develop market-based solutions that will contribute to universal sanitation coverage in six provinces (Svay Rieng, Kandal, Prey Veng, Kampong Thom, Siem Reap and Oddar Meanchey) - reducing stunting among children and, preventing the spread of disease and contamination of drinking water. This supports the Cambodian governments aim of eliminating open defecation by 2025five years ahead of the Sustainable Development Goals target of 2030.

title: Anti-Trafficking in Persons Project [through International Justice Mission]
description: The International Justice Mission (IJM) will implement its police training program in Kratie and Sihanoukville.  It will also create a replicable program in Phnom Penh aimed at empowering and investing in survivors of commercial sexual exploitation (CSE) who, through support and guidance of IJM aftercare partners, have reached a high level of recovery and have expressed the desire to assist newly rescued CSE victims. Participants will be empowered as leaders and educators in their communities, provide crisis care and mentorship to newly rescued victims, and assist in preventing trafficking in high risk areas.

title: Anti-Trafficking in Persons Project [through World Hope International]
description: World Hope International will implement a satellite assessment center in Siem Reap, based on its G/TIP funded assessment and aftercare center in Phnom Penh.  The organization will provide comprehensive services for girl survivors of commercial sexual exploitation and rape. Services will include medical and mental health assessments, art therapy, and assistance with preparing for court proceedings, with the goal of recovery and integration into healthy communities.  The project will also conduct staff training.

title: Asian Elephant Conservation Fund
description: The purpose of this project is to: 1) Continue delivery of education curriculum to rural schools in the Cardamom Mountains and expand this outreach into national schools in Kompong Som and Phnom Penh, focusing on threats to Cambodia's flagship species, 2) Continue capacity and understanding of key environmental issues among teachers, community educators, and community leaders through training, staff development, monitoring and evaluation, and provide multiple-use long lasting educational materials, 3) Complement environmental education awareness of both rural students and community members to reinforce lessons from the classroom through an anticipated 20 field trips to Phnom Tamao Wildlife Rescue Center for students and community members from around the country, 4) Continue building environmental awareness and pride in Cambodia's natural heritage among students and communities through interactive hands-on Community Night Shows, which complement our work in schools. A minimum of 15 Community Night Shows will be conducted in the coming project year in Koh Kong and beyond, 5) Raise community awareness among Cambodians on a nationwide level regarding the devastating effects of the illegal wildlife trade, destruction of habitats, and other factors threatening Cambodia's wildlife through large-scale signage and outreach activities via collaboration and engagement with national ministries, NGOs, and other institutions, 6) Complement conservation awareness-raising and large signage outreach efforts by installing matching signs and hotline stickers on 10 tuk-tuks in Phnom Penh for one year, publicizing the illegality of trading wildlife and promoting Wildlife Alliance's 24-hour nationwide wildlife crime hotline.

title: Great Apes Conservation Fund
description: The purpose of this proposal is to deliver an education curriculum that includes information regarding wildlife and forestry laws and information that will enable Cambodians to make informed decisions regarding the sustainable management of their natural resources while promoting protection of areas rich in biodiversity. This will be done by: 1) delivering a gibbon-focused environmental curriculum to students (3,000), teachers (200), community members, and community leaders in Koh Kong, Kompong Som, and Phnom Penh, 2) conducting at least 15 conservation oriented Community Night Shows and 20 field trips to Phnom Tamao Wildlife Rescue Center (PTWRC), 3) conducting follow up visits to each school to ensure that teachers are delivering the environmental education lessons and to provide them continuing support in doing that, 6) expanding the Kouprey Express' partnership network to provinces not previously addressed, and 7) renewing existing signs and installing new, high visibility multi-lingual billboards and double-sided overhead signs at highly trafficked intersections having conservation messages targeting illegal trafficking of wildlife.

title: Continuing Pileated Gibbon Conservation Education and Public Outreach in Cambodia through the Kouprey Express
description: The project will accomplish the following objectives: (1) Continue building capacity and understanding of key environmental issues for 300 teachers, community educators, and community leaders in communities, schools and NGOs in target areas as well as all other provinces through training, staff development, monitoring and evaluation, (2) Bring a gibbon-focused education curriculum to an estimated 7,500 students at national schools and NGOs around the country and in the Cardamom Mountains, (3) Conduct an anticipated 20 field trips to Phnom Tamao Wildlife Rescue Center to complement classroom lessons and environmental education awareness outreach activities for students and community members from around the country, (4) Build environmental awareness and pride in Cambodia's natural heritage among students and communities through interactive hands-on Community Night Shows, which complement our work in schools, (5) Continue collaboration with other conservation NGOs on capacity building to help facilitate their own environmental education teams as a means of ensuring our message continues, (6) Continue to conduct Wildlife ID and anti-smuggling training with new Customs and Excise officers from Phnom Penh and Siem Reap International Airports and other relevant agencies, and, (7) Raise community awareness among Cambodians on a nationwide level regarding the devastating effects of the illegal wildlife trade with a focus on gibbons, destruction of habitats, and other factors threatening Cambodia's wildlife through large-scale signage and outreach activities in collaboration with others.

title: Feed the Future Cambodia Harvest II activity - Agricultural Enabling Environment
description: Feed the Future Cambodia Harvest II (Harvest II) builds upon years of USAID investment, including the Helping Address Rural Vulnerabilities and Ecosystem Stability (HARVEST) program, which demonstrated success in increasing horticultural production and strengthening private input supply networks. Continuing to work across the Feed the Future zone of influence (ZOI) in the provinces of Pursat, Battambang, Siem Reap, and Kampong Thom, Harvest II will devote particular attention to building market linkages. It will use a buyer-led approach and will support expansion of commercial partnerships that will ultimately allow horticultural producers and buyers to compete more effectively in domestic and international markets. To increase sustainable economic opportunities within a market-based and inclusive horticulture sector, Harvest II has three interconnected sub-purposes: Improve capacities for market participation, Improve market linkages, and Improve governance and enabling environment.

title: Feed the Future HARVEST II
description: Feed the Future Cambodia Harvest II builds on the results and adopts lessons learned from the HARVEST I activity and is in its second year of implementation. title: Cambodia Rural Sanitation Development Impact Bond Activity
description: A groundbreaking initiative to bring safe sanitation to some of the poorest and most vulnerable households in Cambodia launches today. The Cambodia Rural Sanitation DIB is the worlds first Development Impact Bond for sanitation and aims to eradicate the high rates of open defecation in the country and accelerate the Cambodian governments efforts to reach universal sanitation. The DIB aims to develop market-based solutions that will contribute to universal sanitation coverage in six provinces (Svay Rieng, Kandal, Prey Veng, Kampong Thom, Siem Reap and Oddar Meanchey) - reducing stunting among children and, preventing the spread of disease and contamination of drinking water. This supports the Cambodian governments aim of eliminating open defecation by 2025five years ahead of the Sustainable Development Goals target of 2030.

title: Feed the Future Cambodia Harvest II activity - Agricultural Enabling Environment
description: Feed the Future Cambodia Harvest II (Harvest II) builds upon years of USAID investment, including the Helping Address Rural Vulnerabilities and Ecosystem Stability (HARVEST) program, which demonstrated success in increasing horticultural production and strengthening private input supply networks. Continuing to work across the Feed the Future zone of influence (ZOI) in the provinces of Pursat, Battambang, Siem Reap, and Kampong Thom, Harvest II will devote particular attention to building market linkages. It will use a buyer-led approach and will support expansion of commercial partnerships that will ultimately allow horticultural producers and buyers to compete more effectively in domestic and international markets. To increase sustainable economic opportunities within a market-based and inclusive horticulture sector, Harvest II has three interconnected sub-purposes: Improve capacities for market participation, Improve market linkages, and Improve governance and enabling environment.

It will accelerate growth in the fruits and vegetable sector across the Global Food Security Strategy's Zone of Influence in the provinces of Pursat, Battambang, Siem Reap and Kampong Thom. Harvest II focuses on building market linkages using a buyer-led, market system approach and support commercial relationships that will ultimately allow producers, buyers, farmer groups, and collectors to compete more effectively in domestic and international markets. This activity will increase investment and sales as well as create new jobs in the agriculture sector. Harvest II will also work to create a better enabling environment for investment and trade in the sector, foster public private dialogue to address the constraints to agricultural growth, and, recognize the importance of women and youth participation. Harvest II focuses on market systems development and is contributing to the Global Food Security Strategy goal to sustainably reduce poverty, hunger, and malnutrition. The activity falls under the Administration priority to foster economic opportunities for the American people by improving supply chain management, promoting private sector productivity, and leveraging private sector partnerships. In addition, the activity contributes to Mission Objective 4.2 (CDCS DO3) - Strengthen sustainable and resilient pathways out of poverty. The activity was awarded through a competitive process in which the offeror with the best value to the U.S. government was selected, in accordance with federal procurement regulations..

title: Feed the Future Cambodia Harvest II activity - Agricultural Enabling Environment
description: Feed the Future Cambodia Harvest II (Harvest II) builds upon years of USAID investment, including the Helping Address Rural Vulnerabilities and Ecosystem Stability (HARVEST) program, which demonstrated success in increasing horticultural production and strengthening private input supply networks. Continuing to work across the Feed the Future zone of influence (ZOI) in the provinces of Pursat, Battambang, Siem Reap, and Kampong Thom, Harvest II will devote particular attention to building market linkages. It will use a buyer-led approach and will support expansion of commercial partnerships that will ultimately allow horticultural producers and buyers to compete more effectively in domestic and international markets. To increase sustainable economic opportunities within a market-based and inclusive horticulture sector, Harvest II has three interconnected sub-purposes: Improve capacities for market participation, Improve market linkages, and Improve governance and enabling environment.

title: Cambodia Rural Sanitation Development Impact Bond Activity
description: A groundbreaking initiative to bring safe sanitation to some of the poorest and most vulnerable households in Cambodia launches today. The Cambodia Rural Sanitation DIB is the worlds first Development Impact Bond for sanitation and aims to eradicate the high rates of open defecation in the country and accelerate the Cambodian governments efforts to reach universal sanitation. The DIB aims to develop market-based solutions that will contribute to universal sanitation coverage in six provinces (Svay Rieng, Kandal, Prey Veng, Kampong Thom, Siem Reap and Oddar Meanchey) - reducing stunting among children and, preventing the spread of disease and contamination of drinking water. This supports the Cambodian governments aim of eliminating open defecation by 2025five years ahead of the Sustainable Development Goals target of 2030.

title: Feed the Future Cambodia Rice Field Fisheries II
description: Rice field fisheries (RFF), defined as the fishing done in and around rice fields, particularly during the flood season, are a vital source of income and nutrition for Cambodias poor farmers. To increase productivity and maintain biodiversity of wild fish in RFF, the project works in the Tonle Sap floodplain to improve management of community fish refuges (CFR), which provide dry season sanctuaries for broodstock. Building on phase I, the project focuses on replicating and scaling up best practices for CFR management, including efficient water use and integration with food crops, and promoting the nutritional benefits of consuming fish.

title: Roost Protection And Habitat Creation For The White-Shouldered Ibis In Northern Cambodia
description: This project will promote a stable or increasing population of White-shouldered Ibis in Western Siem Pang Forest and Lomphat Wildlife Sanctuary. The grantee will undertake an innovative method to create additional habitat, specific objectives include: (1) Playback of bird calls, (2) The use of dolly (model) birds to encourage live birds to join new communal roosting sites, (3) The enhancement of preferred White-shouldered Ibis foraging habitat by the digging of forest pools trapeangs as key foraging resources for the species.

title: Reducing Trafficking of Cambodia's Cantor's Giant Softshelled Turtle
description: The purpose of this project is to counter endangered turtle trafficking in Kratie and Stung Treng provinces, Cambodia, by building upon a currently successful model of community and local government engagement. This project is intended to conserve the endangered 'Cantor's Giant Softshelled Turtle', pelochelys cantorii, by addressing the impacts of local consumption and international trade of the turtles and their eggs. Specific activities will include: (1) engage community members with high community standing as Turtle Ambassadors to participate in adult/fisher education sessions and patrols in current target sites, (2) extending the efforts of current Community Rangers, (3) extending and expanding our community education program in current target sites, and (4) rollout of project activities in a newly identified hunting hotspot.

title: Feed the Future HARVEST II
description: Feed the Future Cambodia Harvest II builds on the results and adopts lessons learned from the HARVEST I activity and is in its second year of implementation. It will accelerate growth in the fruits and vegetable sector across the Global Food Security Strategy's Zone of Influence in the provinces of Pursat, Battambang, Siem Reap and Kampong Thom. Harvest II focuses on building market linkages using a buyer-led, market system approach and support commercial relationships that will ultimately allow producers, buyers, farmer groups, and collectors to compete more effectively in domestic and international markets. This activity will increase investment and sales as well as create new jobs in the agriculture sector. Harvest II will also work to create a better enabling environment for investment and trade in the sector, foster public private dialogue to address the constraints to agricultural growth, and, recognize the importance of women and youth participation. Harvest II focuses on market systems development and is contributing to the Global Food Security Strategy goal to sustainably reduce poverty, hunger, and malnutrition. The activity falls under the Administration priority to foster economic opportunities for the American people by improving supply chain management, promoting private sector productivity, and leveraging private sector partnerships. In addition, the activity contributes to Mission Objective 4.2 (CDCS DO3) - Strengthen sustainable and resilient pathways out of poverty. title: Cambodia Rural Sanitation Development Impact Bond Activity
description: A groundbreaking initiative to bring safe sanitation to some of the poorest and most vulnerable households in Cambodia launches today. The Cambodia Rural Sanitation DIB is the worlds first Development Impact Bond for sanitation and aims to eradicate the high rates of open defecation in the country and accelerate the Cambodian governments efforts to reach universal sanitation. The DIB aims to develop market-based solutions that will contribute to universal sanitation coverage in six provinces (Svay Rieng, Kandal, Prey Veng, Kampong Thom, Siem Reap and Oddar Meanchey) - reducing stunting among children and, preventing the spread of disease and contamination of drinking water. This supports the Cambodian governments aim of eliminating open defecation by 2025five years ahead of the Sustainable Development Goals target of 2030.

title: Cambodia Rural Sanitation Development Impact Bond Activity
description: A groundbreaking initiative to bring safe sanitation to some of the poorest and most vulnerable households in Cambodia launches today. The Cambodia Rural Sanitation DIB is the worlds first Development Impact Bond for sanitation and aims to eradicate the high rates of open defecation in the country and accelerate the Cambodian governments efforts to reach universal sanitation. The DIB aims to develop market-based solutions that will contribute to universal sanitation coverage in six provinces (Svay Rieng, Kandal, Prey Veng, Kampong Thom, Siem Reap and Oddar Meanchey) - reducing stunting among children and, preventing the spread of disease and contamination of drinking water. This supports the Cambodian governments aim of eliminating open defecation by 2025five years ahead of the Sustainable Development Goals target of 2030.

title: Direct protection to Asia's last intact elephant corridor, Cambodia
description: The Southern Cardamom Forest Protection Program (SCFPP) implements a direct, holistic approach to forest protection in Cambodia, providing ranger patrols which protect wild Asian elephants and their habitats from poaching and land encroachment in this landscape. This project will protect Asian elephants by improving ranger effectiveness through training, strengthen good governance by building strong cases and following-up with the courts on active cases, provide investigative skill development training, and create better linkages between remote villages and ranger stations to address land encroachment. SCFPP rangers will conduct daily forest patrols to effectively resolve human-elephant conflicts, operate ranger stations, and preserve the forests of the Southern Cardamom Mountains of Cambodia.

title: Direct Protection to Asia's Last Intact Elephant Corridor.
description: This project endeavors to protect wild Asian elephants in the Southern Cardamom Mountains of Cambodia from poaching, prevent forest fragmentation and encroachment, and preserve continuous forest cover for elephant movement. Project activities include: 1) conduct capacity building and professionalization training for forest rangers in order for increase their effectiveness in cases involving high-ranking officials and middlemen involved in wildlife trafficking, 2) provide legal support in court proceedings, legal documentation procedures, and ensure cases are prosecuted, 3) increase effectiveness of intelligence gathering to obtain information leading to wildlife smuggling rings and logging syndicates, and 4) create better linkages between remote villages and ranger stations to address land encroachment in the elephant corridor. Through forest and wildlife protection via ranger law enforcement and forest protection this project will contribute to the conservation and survival of wild Asian elephants in Cambodia.

title: Reducing Threats to Elephants and Mitigating Human-Elephant Conflict in the Core Habitat of the Cardamom Mountain Landscape, Cambodia
description: The goal of this project is to reduce threats to wild Asian elephant conservation and population recovery in the Cardamom Mountain Landscape of Cambodia and support communities in mitigating human-elephant conflict (HEC). Specific projects objectives are: 1) reduce demand for wildlife products, 2) support the government in zoning and demarcation of key elephant habitats, and 3) reduce HEC through sustainable mitigation techniques and local management of HEC at key sites. Project activities include: 1) develop a wildlife products demand reduction campaign, 2) work with government authorities to zone protected areas with a special focus on key elephant habitat and connectivity, 3) support government-led HEC response teams to educate and train local stakeholders in conflict mitigation, 4) support two primary schools within elephant habitat to enable local school children to receive an education and build community support for conservation activities, and 5) investigate and pilot innovative and sustainable methods for HEC mitigation and reduction. This project will contribute to the stabilization and long-term growth of the Asian elephant population in Cambodia.

Activities include: 1) support an effective nationwide demand reduction campaign targeting bushmeat consumption, 2) support community elephant wardens to use camera traps and Spatial Monitoring and Reporting Tool (SMART) to monitor elephant presence, threats, and HEC, 3) educate and train local stakeholders in HEC mitigation, 4) establish new government-led HEC response teams, 5) reduce HEC in impacted communities by developing and testing mitigation techniques, and 6) build community support for conservation activities through support to targeted primary schools. This project will contribute to the stabilization and long-term increase of the Asian elephant population in Cambodia.
